# What the kit's errors mean, in plain words

<!-- GENERATED by `python3 scripts/plain_errors.py render --write` from docs/errors/errors.json. Edit the JSON, then regenerate; `scripts/plain_errors.py check` fails when this file drifts. -->

Every refusal or failure the kit can show you, written for someone new to security tooling. Each entry says **what happened**, **why it matters**, **the exact fix**, and where to read more. The state's exact name is in brackets after the plain sentence: it is the word to search for in a log, and the word to quote when you ask for help.

In a run, the same sentence is the title of the annotation at the top of the run page and the first line of "What happened, in plain words" in the job's summary. New to the kit? Start with [Getting started in 1 hour](../adoption/GETTING_STARTED_1_HOUR.md).

## advisory_cause

### COVERAGE_PARTIAL (advisory_cause)

A scanner checked most of the code but could not read some files (for example files with syntax it could not parse). **[COVERAGE_PARTIAL]**

- **Why it matters:** The files it skipped were not checked, so the result covers less than the whole repository.
- **Fix:** Open the scanner's job summary: it lists the files it could not read. Fix their syntax, or accept the gap; it does not block.
- **More:** [docs/security-review/READING-THE-RUN-SUMMARY.md](../security-review/READING-THE-RUN-SUMMARY.md)

### FINDINGS_NOT_BLOCKED (advisory_cause)

The scan found issues that do not block at this repository's current enforcement level (crawl or walk). **[FINDINGS_NOT_BLOCKED]**

- **Why it matters:** They are real findings; at a stricter level the same findings would stop the merge.
- **Fix:** Read the findings in the run summary and fix or ticket them while they are cheap to fix.
- **More:** [docs/security-review/READING-THE-RUN-SUMMARY.md](../security-review/READING-THE-RUN-SUMMARY.md)

### KEV_UNAVAILABLE (advisory_cause)

The list of known-exploited vulnerabilities (the CISA KEV catalog) could not be read on this run, so that check did not happen. **[KEV_UNAVAILABLE]**

- **Why it matters:** The run still passes, but nobody confirmed your dependencies are free of actively exploited vulnerabilities.
- **Fix:** Re-run later; if it persists, the platform team checks the network path to the catalog or the organisation feed mirror.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/FEED_MIRRORS.md](../adoption/FEED_MIRRORS.md)

### KNOWN_EXPLOITED_EXCEPTION_ATTRIBUTED (advisory_cause)

A dependency has a vulnerability that attackers are known to exploit, and an approved, ticketed exception covers it for now. **[KNOWN_EXPLOITED_EXCEPTION_ATTRIBUTED]**

- **Why it matters:** Known-exploited vulnerabilities block by default; this one passes only because a named person accepted it until a date.
- **Fix:** Upgrade the dependency to a fixed version before the exception expires.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### SECRET_EXCEPTION_ATTRIBUTED (advisory_cause)

The scan found secrets, and every one is covered by an approved, ticketed exception that has not expired. **[SECRET_EXCEPTION_ATTRIBUTED]**

- **Why it matters:** This is never a clean result: the secrets exist; a person accepted them for a time.
- **Fix:** Rotate and remove the secrets before the exceptions expire; the exception tickets name the owner.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### VERSION_GAP (advisory_cause)

No scanner the kit carries can read the language or framework version this code targets, so part of the code was not checked. **[VERSION_GAP]**

- **Why it matters:** Unchecked code is allowed in dev and test, but uat and prod refuse it unless a named person accepts the gap.
- **Fix:** Move to a version the kit's scanners support (the summary names it), or ask AppSec to record an attributed exception before you promote to uat/prod.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### VERSION_GAP_UNVERIFIED (advisory_cause)

A scanner may not be able to read the version this code targets; nobody has measured it yet. **[VERSION_GAP_UNVERIFIED]**

- **Why it matters:** The gap is recorded and shown, not enforced, until the kit proves the scanner's range.
- **Fix:** Nothing to do now; if you can, move to a version listed as supported in docs/adoption/USAGE.md.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### WEAKENING_ATTRIBUTED (advisory_cause)

A control is running weaker than the kit's baseline, and a named person approved that with a reason and an expiry date. **[WEAKENING_ATTRIBUTED]**

- **Why it matters:** Approved weakenings are allowed, but they expire; when they do, the run asks for a decision again.
- **Fix:** Nothing now. Before the expiry date, fix the cause or ask the approver to renew it.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### WEAKENING_NOT_APPROVED (advisory_cause)

A control is weakened, but the record approving it is missing a field (reason, owner, approver, reference or expiry). **[WEAKENING_NOT_APPROVED]**

- **Why it matters:** Below uat this is recorded; a uat or prod deploy is refused until the record is complete.
- **Fix:** Fill in all five weakening fields in the workflow inputs, with an approver who is not you.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

## api_boundary

Not failures (nothing to do): `ALLOWED`, `BOUND`, `CANONICAL`, `COMPLETE`, `NOT_ATTEMPTED`, `PUBLISHED`.

### ADVISORY (api_boundary)

Findings existed and were deliberately not blocked at this enforcement level. **[ADVISORY]**

- **Why it matters:** They are real; at a stricter level they would block.
- **Fix:** Read and fix or ticket them.
- **More:** [docs/security-review/READING-THE-RUN-SUMMARY.md](../security-review/READING-THE-RUN-SUMMARY.md)

### BLOCKED (api_boundary)

Same meaning and fix as [`routing_result.BLOCKED`](#blocked-routing_result).

### UNBOUND (api_boundary)

The evidence could not be tied to the exact commit and run that produced it. **[UNBOUND]**

- **Why it matters:** Unbound evidence must not be merged or compared with other runs.
- **Fix:** Re-run; if it repeats, report it to the platform team.
- **More:** [docs/operations/FAILURE_MODES.md](../operations/FAILURE_MODES.md)

### UNDETERMINED (api_boundary)

The kit could not establish the security posture: something it needed did not run or could not be collected. **[UNDETERMINED]**

- **Why it matters:** Undetermined is not a pass.
- **Fix:** Re-run; the summary names what was unavailable.
- **More:** [docs/operations/FAILURE_MODES.md](../operations/FAILURE_MODES.md)

## api_token_preflight

Not failures (nothing to do): `TOKEN_ACCEPTED`.

### API_UNREACHABLE (api_token_preflight)

The runner could not reach the GitHub API at all (DNS, connection or timeout). **[API_UNREACHABLE]**

- **Why it matters:** No check that reads GitHub could run.
- **Fix:** Re-run; if it persists on a self-hosted runner, its administrator checks outbound access to the API host.
- **More:** [docs/operations/FAILURE_MODES.md](../operations/FAILURE_MODES.md)

### JOB_TOKEN_REJECTED (api_token_preflight)

GitHub rejected the workflow's own token (401 Bad credentials). **[JOB_TOKEN_REJECTED]**

- **Why it matters:** Every check that reads GitHub (branch protection, environments, alerts) cannot run.
- **Fix:** If the error URL names api.github.com on a <tenant>.ghe.com host, update the pinned kit SHA (KDEC-027); otherwise an organisation owner checks the IP allow list and Actions permissions.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/SETUP.md](../adoption/SETUP.md)

### ORG_IP_ALLOW_LIST_BLOCKS_RUNNER (api_token_preflight)

The organisation's IP allow list blocks this runner from calling GitHub. **[ORG_IP_ALLOW_LIST_BLOCKS_RUNNER]**

- **Why it matters:** The checks that read GitHub cannot run; it is a platform setting, not your code.
- **Fix:** An organisation owner allows GitHub-hosted runners (Settings > Security > IP allow list > allow GitHub Actions) or uses a listed runner.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/SETUP.md](../adoption/SETUP.md)

### ORG_SSO_BLOCKS_TOKEN (api_token_preflight)

Single sign-on blocked a token, which means a step used a personal or app token instead of the workflow's own token. **[ORG_SSO_BLOCKS_TOKEN]**

- **Why it matters:** The workflow's own token is exempt from SSO; a personal token needs SSO authorisation.
- **Fix:** Remove the personal token from GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN in your workflow, or authorise it for SSO.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/SETUP.md](../adoption/SETUP.md)

### RATE_LIMITED (api_token_preflight)

GitHub rate-limited the workflow's API calls. **[RATE_LIMITED]**

- **Why it matters:** Checks it stopped are unknown, never passed.
- **Fix:** Wait for the limit to reset (the log shows when) and re-run.
- **More:** [docs/operations/FAILURE_MODES.md](../operations/FAILURE_MODES.md)

### TOKEN_PREFLIGHT_UNCLASSIFIED (api_token_preflight)

GitHub refused the workflow's token for a reason the kit does not recognise (a missing scope, a 404, a server error). **[TOKEN_PREFLIGHT_UNCLASSIFIED]**

- **Why it matters:** The checks that read GitHub cannot be trusted.
- **Fix:** Read the step log for the HTTP status; most often the job's permissions: block lacks a scope. Compare it with the template.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/SETUP.md](../adoption/SETUP.md)

## artifact_identity

Not failures (nothing to do): `CONTENT_DIGEST_PROVEN`, `LOCAL_BUILD_ONLY`, `REGISTRY_IDENTITY_PROVEN`.

### IDENTITY_UNVERIFIED (artifact_identity)

The image was pushed, but the kit could not prove the pushed image is the one it scanned. **[IDENTITY_UNVERIFIED]**

- **Why it matters:** Deploying an image nobody can tie to its scan would ship unchecked bytes; deploys are refused.
- **Fix:** Re-run the build; if it repeats, check the registry login and that nothing else pushes the same tag.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/PROVENANCE_AND_ATTESTATION.md](../architecture/PROVENANCE_AND_ATTESTATION.md)

### NOT_ESTABLISHED (artifact_identity)

The build never got far enough to establish which image it produced. **[NOT_ESTABLISHED]**

- **Why it matters:** There is nothing to deploy.
- **Fix:** Fix the earlier failure in the build job and re-run.
- **More:** [docs/operations/FAILURE_MODES.md](../operations/FAILURE_MODES.md)

### SITE_DIGEST_MISMATCH (artifact_identity)

The static site about to be released is not byte-for-byte the one that was checked and approved. **[SITE_DIGEST_MISMATCH]**

- **Why it matters:** A changed, added or renamed file is a different release; nothing was deployed.
- **Fix:** Re-run the workflow from the merge so the package, attestation and deploy come from the same build.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

## attestation_verification

Not failures (nothing to do): `ATTESTATION_VERIFIED`.

### ATTESTATION_ABSENT (attestation_verification)

No signed build record (attestation) exists for this image. **[ATTESTATION_ABSENT]**

- **Why it matters:** Nobody can prove where the image came from; advisory at crawl, a decision above it.
- **Fix:** Build the image through the kit's build workflow (it signs every image) instead of pushing it by hand.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/PROVENANCE_AND_ATTESTATION.md](../architecture/PROVENANCE_AND_ATTESTATION.md)

### ATTESTATION_CONTRADICTED (attestation_verification)

The image's signed build record does not match (wrong signature, image, builder or type). **[ATTESTATION_CONTRADICTED]**

- **Why it matters:** This may mean the image was tampered with; it always blocks.
- **Fix:** Do not deploy it. Rebuild from main through the kit's build workflow and tell AppSec about the mismatch.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/PROVENANCE_AND_ATTESTATION.md](../architecture/PROVENANCE_AND_ATTESTATION.md)

### ATTESTATION_HELD_BY_PLAN (attestation_verification)

This private repository's GitHub plan does not offer attestations, so the signature check was skipped. **[ATTESTATION_HELD_BY_PLAN]**

- **Why it matters:** It is recorded as a known gap of the plan, not a failure.
- **Fix:** Nothing for you. On Enterprise Cloud, set the repository variable ATTESTATIONS_AVAILABLE to true.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/PROVENANCE_AND_ATTESTATION.md](../architecture/PROVENANCE_AND_ATTESTATION.md)

### ATTESTATION_NOT_ESTABLISHABLE (attestation_verification)

The image's signed build record could not be checked (the service was unreachable or the verifier missing). **[ATTESTATION_NOT_ESTABLISHABLE]**

- **Why it matters:** An unchecked signature is not a pass.
- **Fix:** Re-run; if it persists, check the runner can reach the GitHub attestations API.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/PROVENANCE_AND_ATTESTATION.md](../architecture/PROVENANCE_AND_ATTESTATION.md)

## authorization_probe_outcome

Not failures (nothing to do): `REFUSED`.

### NOT_FOUND (authorization_probe_outcome)

A scope the check was told to probe does not exist. **[NOT_FOUND]**

- **Why it matters:** It proves nothing about the identity's rights either way.
- **Fix:** Correct the scope id in the check's inputs.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/SETUP.md](../adoption/SETUP.md)

### REACHED (authorization_probe_outcome)

The identity could act on a scope it should have been refused (its rights are wider than declared). **[REACHED]**

- **Why it matters:** This is the loudest failure: the boundary does not hold.
- **Fix:** Ask the identity's owner to remove the role assignment on the scope the summary names.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/SETUP.md](../adoption/SETUP.md)

### UNAVAILABLE (authorization_probe_outcome)

The access check never got an answer (throttling, network or an expired sign-in). **[UNAVAILABLE]**

- **Why it matters:** Unknown is never treated as refused.
- **Fix:** Re-run verify-azure-oidc.yml; check the runner's network if it repeats.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/SETUP.md](../adoption/SETUP.md)

## capability_floor_state

Not failures (nothing to do): `HELD`.

### BREACHED (capability_floor_state)

A scanner that every run must include produced no result, or was removed without a recorded decision. **[BREACHED]**

- **Why it matters:** The kit refuses to report on a run missing a required check.
- **Fix:** Re-run; if it persists, the kit copy may be broken or out of date: update the pinned kit SHA or tell the platform team.
- **More:** [docs/operations/FAILURE_MODES.md](../operations/FAILURE_MODES.md)

### GAP_DECIDED (capability_floor_state)

A required scanner was removed under an approved, time-limited decision, and nothing replaces it yet. **[GAP_DECIDED]**

- **Why it matters:** That coverage is missing on purpose for now; it does not block.
- **Fix:** Nothing for you; the platform team owns the replacement before the decision expires.
- **More:** [docs/operations/FAILURE_MODES.md](../operations/FAILURE_MODES.md)

## code_finding_key_state

Not failures (nothing to do): `CODE_KEYED`, `SECRET_KEYED`.

### RULE_FAMILY_UNKNOWN (code_finding_key_state)

A scanner rule is not in the kit's rule-family table, so its finding has no ticket key. **[RULE_FAMILY_UNKNOWN]**

- **Why it matters:** The kit never guesses a family; the rule is routed to a person to map.
- **Fix:** Nothing for you; the platform team adds the alias (the refusal names the tool and rule).
- **More:** [docs/architecture/TICKETING_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/TICKETING_CONTRACT.md)

### SECRET_FINGERPRINT_NOT_ESTABLISHED (code_finding_key_state)

A secret finding's location could not be read, so it has no ticket key yet. **[SECRET_FINGERPRINT_NOT_ESTABLISHED]**

- **Why it matters:** It still blocks; it is ticketed once it can be read.
- **Fix:** Make sure the checkout is the scanned commit (the default template does); re-run.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/TICKETING_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/TICKETING_CONTRACT.md)

### SOURCE_LINE_EMPTY (code_finding_key_state)

A finding points at a blank or comment line, so it anchors nothing. **[SOURCE_LINE_EMPTY]**

- **Why it matters:** An empty line cannot identify code.
- **Fix:** Nothing; the finding keeps its other identity.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/TICKETING_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/TICKETING_CONTRACT.md)

### SOURCE_LINE_OUT_OF_RANGE (code_finding_key_state)

A finding names a line past the end of the file, so the checkout is not the scanned commit. **[SOURCE_LINE_OUT_OF_RANGE]**

- **Why it matters:** No anchor is taken from another commit's text.
- **Fix:** Re-run on the same commit the scan ran on.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/TICKETING_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/TICKETING_CONTRACT.md)

### SOURCE_NOT_AVAILABLE (code_finding_key_state)

The file a finding names is not in the checkout, so its code anchor could not be read. **[SOURCE_NOT_AVAILABLE]**

- **Why it matters:** The finding stands; only its location anchor is missing.
- **Fix:** Nothing usually; check the scanned path exists in the repository.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/TICKETING_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/TICKETING_CONTRACT.md)

### SOURCE_PATH_REFUSED (code_finding_key_state)

A finding names a path outside the repository, so the kit refused to read it. **[SOURCE_PATH_REFUSED]**

- **Why it matters:** A scanner's path is data and never reaches outside the scanned tree.
- **Fix:** Report the scanner and rule to the platform team.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/TICKETING_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/TICKETING_CONTRACT.md)

## control_weakening

Not failures (nothing to do): `EXCEPTION_ATTRIBUTION`, `NOT_A_CONTROL_SURFACE`, `WEAKENING_ATTRIBUTED`, `WEAKENING_AT_BASELINE`.

### CONTROL_DISABLED (control_weakening)

A workflow input switched a security check off, so it did not run. **[CONTROL_DISABLED]**

- **Why it matters:** Nothing looked at that part of the code, so problems there go unseen.
- **Fix:** Remove the input that disables it (the summary names it); the kit ships every check on.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### CONTROL_RECONFIGURED (control_weakening)

A control's settings differ from the kit's baseline in a way the kit cannot rank as weaker or stronger. **[CONTROL_RECONFIGURED]**

- **Why it matters:** The change may weaken the check; a person should say whether it is intended.
- **Fix:** Remove the custom setting, or record the decision with the five weakening fields.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### CONTROL_SURFACE_DEAD (control_weakening)

A workflow input you set is not read by anything, so setting it has no effect. **[CONTROL_SURFACE_DEAD]**

- **Why it matters:** You may believe a check is configured when it is not.
- **Fix:** Remove the input (the summary names it) and use the one docs/adoption/USAGE.md lists.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### GATE_SOFTENED (control_weakening)

A workflow input lets a scanner report without blocking (for example soft_fail_sast: true). **[GATE_SOFTENED]**

- **Why it matters:** The scanner still looks, but its findings can no longer stop a bad change.
- **Fix:** Remove the soft-fail input from your workflow, or record why with the five weakening fields.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### SCOPE_NARROWED (control_weakening)

A workflow input narrowed what a check looks at (fewer paths, languages or ecosystems). **[SCOPE_NARROWED]**

- **Why it matters:** Code outside the narrowed scope was not checked.
- **Fix:** Remove the narrowing input, or record why with the five weakening fields.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### SEVERITY_RAISED (control_weakening)

A workflow input raised the severity at which a finding counts, so fewer findings act. **[SEVERITY_RAISED]**

- **Why it matters:** Findings below the new threshold were seen and ignored.
- **Fix:** Restore the default threshold, or record why with the five weakening fields.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### TARGET_NOT_SUPPLIED (control_weakening)

A check needs something to look at (an image or an SBOM path) and the workflow did not give it one. **[TARGET_NOT_SUPPLIED]**

- **Why it matters:** The check could not run; that part was not examined.
- **Fix:** Pass the missing input the summary names, or leave it if this repository has no such artefact.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### WEAKENING_EXCEPTION_EXPIRED (control_weakening)

An approved weakening has passed its expiry date. **[WEAKENING_EXCEPTION_EXPIRED]**

- **Why it matters:** Approvals never renew by silence; the run asks for a decision again.
- **Fix:** Fix the cause and remove the weakening, or ask the approver for a new expiry date.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### WEAKENING_IN_FORCE (control_weakening)

A control runs weaker than the kit's baseline on this run. **[WEAKENING_IN_FORCE]**

- **Why it matters:** A weaker control lets more through; the run records it and asks who decided.
- **Fix:** Remove the weakening input, or add the five weakening fields with a named approver.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### WEAKENING_NOT_APPROVED (control_weakening)

Same meaning and fix as [`advisory_cause.WEAKENING_NOT_APPROVED`](#weakening_not_approved-advisory_cause).

### WEAKENING_SELF_APPROVED (control_weakening)

The person named as approver of a weakening is the person who asked for it (or the author of the change). **[WEAKENING_SELF_APPROVED]**

- **Why it matters:** Approving your own exception is never accepted: the gate blocks and every deploy refuses.
- **Fix:** Ask someone on the approver list who is not you to approve it, and put their name in weakening_approver.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### WEAKENING_UNATTRIBUTED (control_weakening)

A control is weakened and nobody recorded why or who decided. **[WEAKENING_UNATTRIBUTED]**

- **Why it matters:** An unexplained weakening is a decision nobody made, so the run asks for one (DECISION_REQUIRED).
- **Fix:** Add weakening_reason and weakening_authority (and the other three fields) to the workflow inputs, or remove the weakening.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

## coverage_state

Not failures (nothing to do): `FULL`.

### COVERAGE_UNDETERMINED (coverage_state)

The kit could not work out how much of the code it can check. **[COVERAGE_UNDETERMINED]**

- **Why it matters:** Coverage is unknown, not complete.
- **Fix:** Re-run; if it persists, send the discover job's log to the platform team.
- **More:** [docs/operations/FAILURE_MODES.md](../operations/FAILURE_MODES.md)

### UNSUPPORTED_PRESENT (coverage_state)

This repository has code in a language the kit has no scanner for, and it was not scanned. **[UNSUPPORTED_PRESENT]**

- **Why it matters:** That code is unchecked.
- **Fix:** Ask the platform team whether a scanner exists for it; until then, review it by hand.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

## dependabot_triage_rule

Not failures (nothing to do): `all_conditions_met`, `not_dependabot`, `wrong_trigger`.

### actions_major_unknown (dependabot_triage_rule)

A GitHub Actions update's version jump could not be read. **[actions_major_unknown]**

- **Why it matters:** Unknown is never treated as safe.
- **Fix:** Review and merge it yourself.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md](../adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md)

### actions_pin_not_sha (dependabot_triage_rule)

A GitHub Actions update is not pinned to a full commit SHA. **[actions_pin_not_sha]**

- **Why it matters:** Actions must be pinned by SHA.
- **Fix:** Pin the action by SHA in the PR, then merge.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md](../adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md)

### breaking_change_signal (dependabot_triage_rule)

The release notes mention a breaking change. **[breaking_change_signal]**

- **Why it matters:** A breaking change needs a person.
- **Fix:** Read the notes, test, and merge it yourself.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md](../adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md)

### compatibility_low (dependabot_triage_rule)

The compatibility score is below this repository's minimum. **[compatibility_low]**

- **Why it matters:** Low-scoring updates often break.
- **Fix:** Test it and merge it yourself.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md](../adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md)

### compatibility_unknown (dependabot_triage_rule)

No compatibility score is available and this repository requires one. **[compatibility_unknown]**

- **Why it matters:** Unknown compatibility is not safe.
- **Fix:** Review and merge it yourself.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md](../adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md)

### critical_ecosystem (dependabot_triage_rule)

The update is in a protected ecosystem (docker, terraform, helm ...). **[critical_ecosystem]**

- **Why it matters:** Infrastructure updates can change runtime behaviour.
- **Fix:** Review and merge it yourself.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md](../adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md)

### critical_package (dependabot_triage_rule)

The package is on the protected list (runtime-critical). **[critical_package]**

- **Why it matters:** Critical packages always get a person.
- **Fix:** Review the changelog and merge it yourself.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md](../adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md)

### excluded_path (dependabot_triage_rule)

This update touches a path excluded from updates (for example test fixtures), so it was closed. **[excluded_path]**

- **Why it matters:** Fixtures are pinned on purpose.
- **Fix:** If the path should take updates, remove it from excluded_paths.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md](../adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md)

### files_unknown (dependabot_triage_rule)

The list of files this update changes could not be read. **[files_unknown]**

- **Why it matters:** Nobody can show it changes only dependencies.
- **Fix:** Review the diff and merge it yourself.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md](../adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md)

### lockfile_churn (dependabot_triage_rule)

The lockfile changes more lines than this repository auto-merges. **[lockfile_churn]**

- **Why it matters:** Large lockfile changes can hide unrelated moves.
- **Fix:** Review the lockfile diff and merge it yourself.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md](../adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md)

### lockfile_unparsed (dependabot_triage_rule)

The lockfile change could not be read package by package. **[lockfile_unparsed]**

- **Why it matters:** Nobody can show only the named packages moved.
- **Fix:** Review the lockfile diff and merge it yourself.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md](../adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md)

### lockfile_unrelated_moves (dependabot_triage_rule)

The lockfile also changes packages this update does not name. **[lockfile_unrelated_moves]**

- **Why it matters:** Unrelated moves are not covered by the update.
- **Fix:** Review the extra packages and merge it yourself.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md](../adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md)

### maintainer_changed (dependabot_triage_rule)

The package's maintainer changed since the last version. **[maintainer_changed]**

- **Why it matters:** A new maintainer is a supply-chain signal.
- **Fix:** Check the new maintainer and merge it yourself.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md](../adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md)

### major_update (dependabot_triage_rule)

This is a major version update. **[major_update]**

- **Why it matters:** Major versions may break behaviour.
- **Fix:** Read the release notes, test, and merge it yourself.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md](../adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md)

### metadata_unverified (dependabot_triage_rule)

The update's Dependabot metadata could not be verified. **[metadata_unverified]**

- **Why it matters:** Unverified updates are never auto-merged.
- **Fix:** Review and merge it yourself.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md](../adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md)

### no_required_checks (dependabot_triage_rule)

The base branch requires no status checks, so an auto-merge would merge untested code. **[no_required_checks]**

- **Why it matters:** Auto-merge is safe only behind required checks.
- **Fix:** Require "security / Security gate" on main (docs/adoption/BRANCH_PROTECTION_SETTINGS.md).
- **More:** [docs/adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md](../adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md)

### non_dependency_change (dependabot_triage_rule)

The update changes something other than a dependency version. **[non_dependency_change]**

- **Why it matters:** Only version changes may auto-merge.
- **Fix:** Review and merge it yourself.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md](../adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md)

### non_dependency_file (dependabot_triage_rule)

The update changes a file that is not a manifest or lockfile. **[non_dependency_file]**

- **Why it matters:** Only dependency files may auto-merge.
- **Fix:** Review the extra file and merge it yourself.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md](../adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md)

### policy_misconfigured (dependabot_triage_rule)

The triage settings in the caller workflow are invalid, so every update goes to a person. **[policy_misconfigured]**

- **Why it matters:** A broken policy must never auto-merge.
- **Fix:** Fix the triage inputs the comment names in .github/workflows/dependabot-triage.yml.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md](../adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md)

### required_checks_unknown (dependabot_triage_rule)

The branch protection of the base branch could not be read. **[required_checks_unknown]**

- **Why it matters:** Nobody can show the required checks would decide the merge.
- **Fix:** Give the triage token read access, or review and merge yourself.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md](../adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md)

### scan_gate_not_required (dependabot_triage_rule)

A check the triage relies on is not required on the base branch. **[scan_gate_not_required]**

- **Why it matters:** The merge would not wait for it.
- **Fix:** Make the named check required in the branch ruleset.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md](../adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md)

### scan_gate_unnamed (dependabot_triage_rule)

The triage caller names no required_checks. **[scan_gate_unnamed]**

- **Why it matters:** Nothing shows the tests and scan decide the merge.
- **Fix:** Set required_checks in dependabot-triage.yml (for example "security / Security gate").
- **More:** [docs/adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md](../adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md)

### security_critical (dependabot_triage_rule)

This is a security update for a protected package. **[security_critical]**

- **Why it matters:** Security updates to critical packages get a person first, urgently.
- **Fix:** Review it first and merge it today.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md](../adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md)

### triage_chain (dependabot_triage_rule)

The update changes the triage workflow or the kit pin itself. **[triage_chain]**

- **Why it matters:** An update must not decide its own merge.
- **Fix:** Review and merge it yourself.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md](../adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md)

### update_type_not_allowed (dependabot_triage_rule)

The update type is not one this repository auto-merges. **[update_type_not_allowed]**

- **Why it matters:** Only allowed types merge on their own.
- **Fix:** Review and merge it yourself.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md](../adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md)

### update_type_unknown (dependabot_triage_rule)

The update type (major, minor, patch) could not be read. **[update_type_unknown]**

- **Why it matters:** Unknown is never treated as safe.
- **Fix:** Review and merge it yourself.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md](../adoption/DEPENDABOT_TRIAGE.md)

## deploy_coverage

### NO_KIT_ADAPTER (deploy_coverage)

This repository deploys to a kind of hosting the kit has no deploy step for (for example AKS, VMs or code-packaged Functions). **[NO_KIT_ADAPTER]**

- **Why it matters:** The kit scans the code, but its deploy safety checks do not cover that hosting.
- **Fix:** Deploy as a container (Container Apps or App Service) or a static site, or ask the platform team about your hosting.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

## deployment_outcome

Not failures (nothing to do): `DEPLOY_HEALTHY`, `ROLLBACK_TO_EMPTY`.

### DEPLOY_REFUSED (deployment_outcome)

The deploy was refused before it changed anything; the reason is the first refusal listed below it. **[DEPLOY_REFUSED]**

- **Why it matters:** Nothing in the environment was touched, so there is nothing to clean up.
- **Fix:** Read the refusal named in the deploy summary (each has its own entry in this catalogue), fix it, and re-run the deploy.
- **More:** [docs/security-review/READING-THE-RUN-SUMMARY.md](../security-review/READING-THE-RUN-SUMMARY.md)

### MANUAL_RECOVERY_REQUIRED (deployment_outcome)

The deploy failed its checks and could not undo itself automatically; the failed version is still live. **[MANUAL_RECOVERY_REQUIRED]**

- **Why it matters:** A person has to decide how to recover.
- **Fix:** Follow the escalation in the deploy summary (owner and allowed actions), or contact the platform team now.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md)

### PARTIAL_APPLY (deployment_outcome)

The deploy started changing the environment and could not confirm it finished. **[PARTIAL_APPLY]**

- **Why it matters:** Things may exist that no record knows about.
- **Fix:** Do not re-run blindly: ask the platform team to inspect the target (the summary names it) before another deploy.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md)

### ROLLBACK_PARTIAL (deployment_outcome)

The deploy undid part of the change but not all of it. **[ROLLBACK_PARTIAL]**

- **Why it matters:** The environment is in a mixed state.
- **Fix:** Ask the platform team to review the residue listed in the summary before deploying again.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md)

### ROLLBACK_TO_PRIOR (deployment_outcome)

The new version failed its checks and the deploy put the previous version back. **[ROLLBACK_TO_PRIOR]**

- **Why it matters:** Your change is not live; the previous version is.
- **Fix:** Read why the new version failed (health or tests in the summary), fix it and deploy again.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md)

### STATUS_UNTRUSTED (deployment_outcome)

The deploy changed the environment and then lost track of what it changed. **[STATUS_UNTRUSTED]**

- **Why it matters:** Nobody knows the current state; it is neither success nor clean failure.
- **Fix:** Stop deploying to this target and ask the platform team to inspect it.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md)

## discovery_state

Not failures (nothing to do): `ARTIFACT_PRESENT`, `CAPABILITY_REQUIRED`, `NOT_APPLICABLE`, `RUN`.

### COVERAGE_GAP (discovery_state)

Code is present that needs a check, and no scanner looked at it. **[COVERAGE_GAP]**

- **Why it matters:** This is neither clean nor not-applicable: it is unchecked.
- **Fix:** Tell the platform team which kind of file it is (the summary names it); consider a scanner or a manual review.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### DISABLED (discovery_state)

A check was explicitly turned off for this repository. **[DISABLED]**

- **Why it matters:** It is an exception, and it is reported every run.
- **Fix:** Turn it back on, or make sure the exception is recorded with an owner and expiry.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### DISCOVERY_PARTIAL (discovery_state)

Some of the kit's file-type probes failed; the rest worked. **[DISCOVERY_PARTIAL]**

- **Why it matters:** The probes that failed are treated as present, so those scanners run anyway.
- **Fix:** Re-run; if it persists, send the discover job's log to the platform team.
- **More:** [docs/operations/FAILURE_MODES.md](../operations/FAILURE_MODES.md)

### DISCOVERY_UNAVAILABLE (discovery_state)

Same meaning and fix as [`execution_unavailable_reason.DISCOVERY_UNAVAILABLE`](#discovery_unavailable-execution_unavailable_reason).

### EXCLUDED_BY_SELECTOR (discovery_state)

Code of a kind the kit scans is present, but a workflow input excluded it. **[EXCLUDED_BY_SELECTOR]**

- **Why it matters:** That code was not checked.
- **Fix:** Remove the exclusion input, or record why with the five weakening fields.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### MISSING_BUT_REQUIRED (discovery_state)

Something this repository is declared to have (for example infrastructure code) is missing. **[MISSING_BUT_REQUIRED]**

- **Why it matters:** The absence itself is the finding.
- **Fix:** Add the missing part, or correct the declaration (for example iac_mode) in the workflow.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### SCANNER_UNAVAILABLE (discovery_state)

The kit has no scanner for a kind of file found in this repository. **[SCANNER_UNAVAILABLE]**

- **Why it matters:** That code was not checked by anything.
- **Fix:** Nothing for you; the platform team owns adding a scanner (the summary names the kind).
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### UNDETERMINED_PRESENT (discovery_state)

The kit could not tell whether code of one kind is present, so it scans for it anyway. **[UNDETERMINED_PRESENT]**

- **Why it matters:** An unknown is never treated as absent.
- **Fix:** Nothing for you; re-run if the discover job failed.
- **More:** [docs/operations/FAILURE_MODES.md](../operations/FAILURE_MODES.md)

## edge_purge

Not failures (nothing to do): `EDGE_PURGED`, `EDGE_PURGE_NOT_APPLICABLE`.

### EDGE_PURGE_FAILED (edge_purge)

Clearing the edge cache failed after a good release. **[EDGE_PURGE_FAILED]**

- **Why it matters:** Users may see the old version until the cache expires; the release itself stands.
- **Fix:** Purge the endpoint by hand or wait for the cache to expire; check the deploy identity's rights on Front Door.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/LZ_KIT_SEAM_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/LZ_KIT_SEAM_CONTRACT.md)

### EDGE_PURGE_REFUSED (edge_purge)

The edge endpoint the environment names is not a Front Door endpoint, so its cache was not cleared. **[EDGE_PURGE_REFUSED]**

- **Why it matters:** Users may see the old version until the cache expires.
- **Fix:** Ask the platform team to correct KIT_EDGE_ENDPOINT.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/LZ_KIT_SEAM_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/LZ_KIT_SEAM_CONTRACT.md)

## environment_protection

Not failures (nothing to do): `ENVIRONMENT_PROTECTION_NOT_REQUIRED`, `ENVIRONMENT_PROTECTION_VERIFIED`.

### ENVIRONMENT_APPROVERS_ALL_APP_TEAM (environment_protection)

Every reviewer of the uat or prod environment is on the app team that wrote the change. **[ENVIRONMENT_APPROVERS_ALL_APP_TEAM]**

- **Why it matters:** The team cannot approve its own production release; someone from platform or security must be able to; the deploy is refused before sign-in.
- **Fix:** Add the platform or security team as a required reviewer of the environment (Settings > Environments > <env>), keeping Prevent self-review on.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/BRANCH_PROTECTION_SETTINGS.md](../adoption/BRANCH_PROTECTION_SETTINGS.md)

### ENVIRONMENT_APPROVER_GROUP_MISSING (environment_protection)

The environment's reviewers are not from the approver groups the policy names. **[ENVIRONMENT_APPROVER_GROUP_MISSING]**

- **Why it matters:** Someone outside the named groups could approve a production release; refused.
- **Fix:** Set the environment's required reviewers to the groups the summary names (for example platform or security).
- **More:** [docs/adoption/SETUP.md](../adoption/SETUP.md)

### ENVIRONMENT_APPROVER_POOL_MISSING (environment_protection)

None of the uat or prod environment's reviewers is in the platform or security approver pool. **[ENVIRONMENT_APPROVER_POOL_MISSING]**

- **Why it matters:** Approvals for production come from platform or security, outside the app team; the deploy is refused before sign-in.
- **Fix:** Make a platform or security pool team (vars.KIT_APPROVER_POOLS, else approver_pools in .kit/settings.json) a required reviewer of the environment in Settings > Environments > <env>.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/BRANCH_PROTECTION_SETTINGS.md](../adoption/BRANCH_PROTECTION_SETTINGS.md)

### ENVIRONMENT_NOT_FOUND (environment_protection)

The uat or prod environment this deploy names does not exist in the repository. **[ENVIRONMENT_NOT_FOUND]**

- **Why it matters:** Without the environment GitHub has no reviewer to wait for, so a production deploy would need no approval; it is refused before sign-in.
- **Fix:** Create the environment with its reviewers (the gh api -X PUT repos/<repo>/environments/<env> command in .kit/ADOPTION_CHECKLIST.md), or correct the github_environment name in the caller workflow.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/BRANCH_PROTECTION_SETTINGS.md](../adoption/BRANCH_PROTECTION_SETTINGS.md)

### ENVIRONMENT_PROTECTION_NOT_ESTABLISHED (environment_protection)

The deploy could not read the environment's protection rules (or the tier is not registered). **[ENVIRONMENT_PROTECTION_NOT_ESTABLISHED]**

- **Why it matters:** Unknown protection is not protection; refused at uat and prod.
- **Fix:** Check the deploy job has actions: read and that KIT_ENVIRONMENT_TIER is one of sandbox, dev, test, uat, prod.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/SETUP.md](../adoption/SETUP.md)

### ENVIRONMENT_REVIEWERS_ABSENT (environment_protection)

The uat or prod environment has no required reviewers (no required-reviewers rule), so anyone who can run the workflow could deploy. **[ENVIRONMENT_REVIEWERS_ABSENT]**

- **Why it matters:** A production deploy must be approved by someone other than the deployer; the deploy is refused.
- **Fix:** A repository admin adds required reviewers (platform or security) in Settings > Environments > <env>; .kit/ADOPTION_CHECKLIST.md has the gh api command.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/SETUP.md](../adoption/SETUP.md)

### ENVIRONMENT_REVIEWERS_EMPTY (environment_protection)

The uat or prod environment has a required-reviewers rule that names nobody, so nobody is waited for. **[ENVIRONMENT_REVIEWERS_EMPTY]**

- **Why it matters:** A production deploy needs a person from platform or security to approve it; the deploy is refused before sign-in.
- **Fix:** A repository admin adds the platform or security team as a required reviewer in Settings > Environments > <env>; .kit/ADOPTION_CHECKLIST.md has the exact gh api -X PUT command.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/BRANCH_PROTECTION_SETTINGS.md](../adoption/BRANCH_PROTECTION_SETTINGS.md)

### ENVIRONMENT_SELF_REVIEW_ALLOWED (environment_protection)

The environment lets the person who started the deploy approve it themselves. **[ENVIRONMENT_SELF_REVIEW_ALLOWED]**

- **Why it matters:** Self-approval is not an independent check; the deploy is refused.
- **Fix:** Tick "Prevent self-review" in Settings > Environments > <env> (or prevent_self_review: true in the gh api call).
- **More:** [docs/adoption/SETUP.md](../adoption/SETUP.md)

### ENVIRONMENT_UNCLASSED (environment_protection)

The deploy names no environment, or one the kit cannot tell is dev, test, uat or prod. **[ENVIRONMENT_UNCLASSED]**

- **Why it matters:** An environment nobody has classed might be production, so it is refused at every tier rather than deployed without an approval.
- **Fix:** Add the environment to .kit/environments.json with "class": "dev", "test", "uat" or "prod" (kit init writes this file), or use a name with dev, test, uat or prod in it.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/BRANCH_PROTECTION_SETTINGS.md](../adoption/BRANCH_PROTECTION_SETTINGS.md)

## evidence_retention

Not failures (nothing to do): `EVIDENCE_RETENTION_DEFAULT`, `EVIDENCE_RETENTION_SET`.

### EVIDENCE_RETENTION_CAPPED (evidence_retention)

KIT_EVIDENCE_RETENTION_DAYS was above GitHub's 400-day maximum, so 400 was used. **[EVIDENCE_RETENTION_CAPPED]**

- **Why it matters:** GitHub cannot keep artifacts longer.
- **Fix:** Set it to 400 or less.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### EVIDENCE_RETENTION_RAISED_TO_FLOOR (evidence_retention)

KIT_EVIDENCE_RETENTION_DAYS was below the audit minimum (or not a number), so the minimum was used. **[EVIDENCE_RETENTION_RAISED_TO_FLOOR]**

- **Why it matters:** Evidence must be kept long enough for audit.
- **Fix:** Set KIT_EVIDENCE_RETENTION_DAYS to at least the floor (90 by default), or remove it.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

## exception_lifecycle

### EXCEPTION_HISTORY_TAMPERED (exception_lifecycle)

Same meaning and fix as [`policy_resolution.EXCEPTION_HISTORY_TAMPERED`](#exception_history_tampered-policy_resolution).

### EXCEPTION_HISTORY_UNVERIFIED (exception_lifecycle)

Same meaning and fix as [`policy_resolution.EXCEPTION_HISTORY_UNVERIFIED`](#exception_history_unverified-policy_resolution).

### EXCEPTION_RENEWAL_LIMIT (exception_lifecycle)

Same meaning and fix as [`policy_resolution.EXCEPTION_RENEWAL_LIMIT`](#exception_renewal_limit-policy_resolution).

## exception_resurfacing

Not failures (nothing to do): `CHECKED`, `NOTHING_DUE`, `NOTHING_TO_RESURFACE`, `NOT_REQUESTED`, `PLANNED`, `RESURFACED`.

### EXCEPTIONS_DUE (exception_resurfacing)

At least one exception is due or overdue. **[EXCEPTIONS_DUE]**

- **Why it matters:** Each is listed with its ticket.
- **Fix:** Work through the list in the run summary.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### EXCEPTION_DUE_SOON (exception_resurfacing)

An exception expires within the next 14 days. **[EXCEPTION_DUE_SOON]**

- **Why it matters:** When it lapses, the finding blocks or routes again.
- **Fix:** Fix the finding, or ask the approver about renewal before the date.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### EXCEPTION_OVERDUE (exception_resurfacing)

An exception has expired, or its expiry date cannot be read. **[EXCEPTION_OVERDUE]**

- **Why it matters:** An unreadable date has not "not arrived"; the finding is treated normally.
- **Fix:** Fix the finding, or get a new dated approval.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### EXCEPTION_TICKET_MISMATCH (exception_resurfacing)

An exception's Jira ticket does not exist or does not match the register (approver or renewal). **[EXCEPTION_TICKET_MISMATCH]**

- **Why it matters:** Reported, never blocking: the register decides; the ticket should agree.
- **Fix:** Correct the ticket (approver, renewal comment) to match the register.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### NOT_ATTEMPTED (exception_resurfacing)

Resurfacing was asked for but not attempted because a source could not be read. **[NOT_ATTEMPTED]**

- **Why it matters:** Nothing was raised on any ticket.
- **Fix:** Check the register files are readable and re-run.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### NOT_CONFIGURED (exception_resurfacing)

No Jira credential is configured, so due exceptions were listed but not raised on tickets. **[NOT_CONFIGURED]**

- **Why it matters:** The list is still accurate; only the ticket comments are missing.
- **Fix:** Set JIRA_EMAIL, JIRA_TOKEN and JIRA_HOST in the ticketing environment.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/JIRA_AUTH_AND_ROUTING.md](../architecture/JIRA_AUTH_AND_ROUTING.md)

### RESURFACE_FAILED (exception_resurfacing)

Raising a due exception on its ticket failed. **[RESURFACE_FAILED]**

- **Why it matters:** The ticket owner may not see it is due.
- **Fix:** Check the Jira credential and that the tracker is Jira; re-run.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/JIRA_AUTH_AND_ROUTING.md](../architecture/JIRA_AUTH_AND_ROUTING.md)

## execution_state

Not failures (nothing to do): `COMPLETE`.

### COLLECTION_FAILED (execution_state)

Same meaning and fix as [`scanner_state.COLLECTION_FAILED`](#collection_failed-scanner_state).

### FAILED (execution_state)

A scanner job did not finish. **[FAILED]**

- **Why it matters:** Its findings are unknown.
- **Fix:** Re-run the job; if it fails again, send its log to the platform team.
- **More:** [docs/operations/FAILURE_MODES.md](../operations/FAILURE_MODES.md)

### NOT_DECLARED (execution_state)

A scanner job did not say whether it completed. **[NOT_DECLARED]**

- **Why it matters:** The kit never assumes a job completed.
- **Fix:** Re-run; if it repeats, report the job name to the platform team.
- **More:** [docs/operations/FAILURE_MODES.md](../operations/FAILURE_MODES.md)

### NOT_RUN (execution_state)

A scanner job never started (skipped, cancelled or gated off earlier in the run). **[NOT_RUN]**

- **Why it matters:** Nothing was checked by it.
- **Fix:** Look for the earlier job that failed or was cancelled, fix it, and re-run.
- **More:** [docs/operations/FAILURE_MODES.md](../operations/FAILURE_MODES.md)

## execution_unavailable_reason

### ACTION_ACQUISITION_FAILURE (execution_unavailable_reason)

The runner could not download an action the job needs. **[ACTION_ACQUISITION_FAILURE]**

- **Why it matters:** The job never started its checks.
- **Fix:** Re-run; if it persists, check that the organisation allows the action (Settings > Actions > General) and that the kit repository is accessible to this one.
- **More:** [docs/operations/FAILURE_MODES.md](../operations/FAILURE_MODES.md)

### BILLING_EXECUTION_REFUSED (execution_unavailable_reason)

GitHub refused to run the job because of a spending limit or a payment problem. **[BILLING_EXECUTION_REFUSED]**

- **Why it matters:** No scanner ran, so nothing was checked.
- **Fix:** Ask an organisation owner to check Settings > Billing (Actions spending limit), then re-run.
- **More:** [docs/operations/FAILURE_MODES.md](../operations/FAILURE_MODES.md)

### DEPENDENCY_ACQUISITION_UNAVAILABLE (execution_unavailable_reason)

A tool the scanner needs could not be downloaded or did not work. **[DEPENDENCY_ACQUISITION_UNAVAILABLE]**

- **Why it matters:** The scanner could not run.
- **Fix:** Re-run; if it persists, send the job log to the platform team (often a blocked download or a changed checksum).
- **More:** [docs/operations/FAILURE_MODES.md](../operations/FAILURE_MODES.md)

### DISCOVERY_UNAVAILABLE (execution_unavailable_reason)

The kit could not work out which languages and files this repository has. **[DISCOVERY_UNAVAILABLE]**

- **Why it matters:** Without that, every scanner runs, which is slower but safe; nothing is skipped as "not applicable".
- **Fix:** Re-run; if it persists, send the discover job's log to the platform team.
- **More:** [docs/operations/FAILURE_MODES.md](../operations/FAILURE_MODES.md)

### EXECUTION_TIMEOUT (execution_unavailable_reason)

The job ran out of time and was stopped. **[EXECUTION_TIMEOUT]**

- **Why it matters:** The scan did not finish, so its result is unknown.
- **Fix:** Re-run; if it times out again, the repository may be very large: ask the platform team about the timeout or the scan scope.
- **More:** [docs/operations/FAILURE_MODES.md](../operations/FAILURE_MODES.md)

### INFRASTRUCTURE_UNKNOWN (execution_unavailable_reason)

A scanner never ran, for a reason the kit could not identify. **[INFRASTRUCTURE_UNKNOWN]**

- **Why it matters:** Nothing was checked by it.
- **Fix:** Re-run; if it repeats, send the job log to the platform team.
- **More:** [docs/operations/FAILURE_MODES.md](../operations/FAILURE_MODES.md)

### POLICY_REFUSED (execution_unavailable_reason)

An environment protection rule refused to run the job on this branch or ref. **[POLICY_REFUSED]**

- **Why it matters:** The job was stopped before it ran.
- **Fix:** Run it from a branch the environment allows (usually main), or ask an admin to check the environment's deployment branch policy.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/SETUP.md](../adoption/SETUP.md)

## external_findings_pull

Not failures (nothing to do): `DUPLICATE_OF_KIT_FINDING`, `SOURCE_PULLED`.

### NOT_MAPPED (external_findings_pull)

A pulled finding could not be turned into a kit finding (no repository, file or known severity). **[NOT_MAPPED]**

- **Why it matters:** It is listed with the reason, not dropped.
- **Fix:** Map the project to this repository, or triage the listed item by hand.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/EXTERNAL_FINDINGS_SONAR_AIKIDO.md](../adoption/EXTERNAL_FINDINGS_SONAR_AIKIDO.md)

### SOURCE_AUTH_REFUSED (external_findings_pull)

SonarQube or Aikido refused the credentials (401/403). **[SOURCE_AUTH_REFUSED]**

- **Why it matters:** Nothing was read; it is never "no findings".
- **Fix:** Renew the token and update the secret.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/EXTERNAL_FINDINGS_SONAR_AIKIDO.md](../adoption/EXTERNAL_FINDINGS_SONAR_AIKIDO.md)

### SOURCE_HOST_REFUSED (external_findings_pull)

The SonarQube or Aikido host is not https, so no credential was sent. **[SOURCE_HOST_REFUSED]**

- **Why it matters:** Credentials go only over https.
- **Fix:** Use the https URL of the service.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/EXTERNAL_FINDINGS_SONAR_AIKIDO.md](../adoption/EXTERNAL_FINDINGS_SONAR_AIKIDO.md)

### SOURCE_NOT_CONFIGURED (external_findings_pull)

A SonarQube or Aikido secret or setting is missing, so nothing was pulled. **[SOURCE_NOT_CONFIGURED]**

- **Why it matters:** No pull is not "no findings".
- **Fix:** Set the SONAR_* or AIKIDO_* secrets the summary names.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/EXTERNAL_FINDINGS_SONAR_AIKIDO.md](../adoption/EXTERNAL_FINDINGS_SONAR_AIKIDO.md)

### SOURCE_RESPONSE_INVALID (external_findings_pull)

SonarQube or Aikido answered in an unexpected shape. **[SOURCE_RESPONSE_INVALID]**

- **Why it matters:** The answer cannot be trusted as complete.
- **Fix:** Check the host is the right product and version; report it to the platform team.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/EXTERNAL_FINDINGS_SONAR_AIKIDO.md](../adoption/EXTERNAL_FINDINGS_SONAR_AIKIDO.md)

### SOURCE_TRUNCATED (external_findings_pull)

SonarQube or Aikido stopped returning pages before all findings were read. **[SOURCE_TRUNCATED]**

- **Why it matters:** A partial pull is never presented as complete.
- **Fix:** Narrow the project or raise the search depth; re-run.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/EXTERNAL_FINDINGS_SONAR_AIKIDO.md](../adoption/EXTERNAL_FINDINGS_SONAR_AIKIDO.md)

### SOURCE_UNREACHABLE (external_findings_pull)

SonarQube or Aikido could not be reached or answered with an error. **[SOURCE_UNREACHABLE]**

- **Why it matters:** Nothing was read.
- **Fix:** Re-run later; check the host secret and the runner's network.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/EXTERNAL_FINDINGS_SONAR_AIKIDO.md](../adoption/EXTERNAL_FINDINGS_SONAR_AIKIDO.md)

## feed_mirror

Not failures (nothing to do): `MIRROR_CURRENT`, `NOT_CONFIGURED`.

### MIRROR_FALLBACK_UPSTREAM (feed_mirror)

The organisation's mirror was refused, and the public feed was read instead because the repository allows that fallback. **[MIRROR_FALLBACK_UPSTREAM]**

- **Why it matters:** This is an approved exception to the private-only rule; it is recorded so it gets reviewed.
- **Fix:** Nothing to do now; the platform team fixes the mirror (the summary names its cause).
- **More:** [docs/adoption/FEED_MIRRORS.md](../adoption/FEED_MIRRORS.md)

### MIRROR_INTEGRITY_FAILED (feed_mirror)

The organisation's copy of a vulnerability database failed its integrity check (a file does not match its checksum). **[MIRROR_INTEGRITY_FAILED]**

- **Why it matters:** Corrupt or tampered data is never used.
- **Fix:** Tell the platform team; they re-run the mirror refresh and investigate the mismatch.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/FEED_MIRRORS.md](../adoption/FEED_MIRRORS.md)

### MIRROR_STALE (feed_mirror)

The organisation's copy of a vulnerability database has not been refreshed recently enough. **[MIRROR_STALE]**

- **Why it matters:** Old data cannot show your dependencies are free of newly published vulnerabilities, so it is not used.
- **Fix:** Tell the platform team: the feed-mirror refresh workflow has stopped (they re-run reusable-feed-mirror-refresh.yml).
- **More:** [docs/adoption/FEED_MIRRORS.md](../adoption/FEED_MIRRORS.md)

### MIRROR_UNREACHABLE (feed_mirror)

The organisation's copy of a vulnerability database could not be reached from this runner. **[MIRROR_UNREACHABLE]**

- **Why it matters:** A database that cannot be read is not a clean result.
- **Fix:** Run the job on a runner with access to the mirror (vars.KIT_FEED_MIRROR_RUNNER), or ask the platform team to check the private endpoint.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/FEED_MIRRORS.md](../adoption/FEED_MIRRORS.md)

## feed_mirror_refresh

Not failures (nothing to do): `MIRROR_PUBLISHED`.

### MIRROR_PUBLISH_UNVERIFIED (feed_mirror_refresh)

The mirror was uploaded, but reading it back did not show a current, intact copy. **[MIRROR_PUBLISH_UNVERIFIED]**

- **Why it matters:** A publish nobody could read back is not a working mirror.
- **Fix:** Check the storage account and the private endpoint, then re-run the refresh.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/FEED_MIRRORS.md](../adoption/FEED_MIRRORS.md)

### MIRROR_UPSTREAM_INTEGRITY_FAILED (feed_mirror_refresh)

The downloaded vulnerability database does not match its own published checksums. **[MIRROR_UPSTREAM_INTEGRITY_FAILED]**

- **Why it matters:** Corrupt data is never published to the mirror.
- **Fix:** Re-run the refresh; if it persists, report it to the platform team.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/FEED_MIRRORS.md](../adoption/FEED_MIRRORS.md)

### MIRROR_UPSTREAM_STALE (feed_mirror_refresh)

The public vulnerability database itself is older than allowed, so the mirror was not updated from it. **[MIRROR_UPSTREAM_STALE]**

- **Why it matters:** Publishing old data would reset the freshness clock over stale content.
- **Fix:** Re-run the refresh later; if it persists, check the upstream feed's status page.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/FEED_MIRRORS.md](../adoption/FEED_MIRRORS.md)

### MIRROR_UPSTREAM_UNREACHABLE (feed_mirror_refresh)

The public vulnerability database could not be downloaded. **[MIRROR_UPSTREAM_UNREACHABLE]**

- **Why it matters:** The mirror keeps its last good copy, which will go stale if this continues.
- **Fix:** Re-run the refresh; if it persists, check the runner's outbound network access.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/FEED_MIRRORS.md](../adoption/FEED_MIRRORS.md)

## finding_baseline_state

Not failures (nothing to do): `NEW`, `PRE_EXISTING_AGE_NOT_ESTABLISHED`, `PRE_EXISTING_BASELINED`, `PRE_EXISTING_BY_DETECTION_CHANGE`.

### BASELINE_UNAVAILABLE (finding_baseline_state)

The record of findings that already existed (the baseline ledger) could not be read. **[BASELINE_UNAVAILABLE]**

- **Why it matters:** The kit cannot tell new findings from old ones, so it treats them all as new.
- **Fix:** Check the ledger file on the default branch is valid JSON; re-run.
- **More:** [docs/operations/FINDING_CLASSIFICATION.md](../operations/FINDING_CLASSIFICATION.md)

## finding_id_form

### CWE_FORM_UNKNOWN (finding_id_form)

A finding carries a weakness id (CWE) in a form the kit does not recognise. **[CWE_FORM_UNKNOWN]**

- **Why it matters:** The kit never guesses an id; the finding is routed to a person.
- **Fix:** Nothing for you; the platform team adds the form if it is valid.
- **More:** [docs/operations/FINDING_CLASSIFICATION.md](../operations/FINDING_CLASSIFICATION.md)

### VULN_ID_FORM_UNKNOWN (finding_id_form)

A finding carries a vulnerability id the kit does not recognise (not CVE, GHSA or OSV). **[VULN_ID_FORM_UNKNOWN]**

- **Why it matters:** The kit never guesses an id; the finding is routed to a person.
- **Fix:** Nothing for you; the platform team maps it in id-mappings.json.
- **More:** [docs/operations/FINDING_CLASSIFICATION.md](../operations/FINDING_CLASSIFICATION.md)

## human_control_availability

Not failures (nothing to do): `HUMAN_CONTROL_AVAILABLE`.

### HUMAN_CONTROL_NO_SEPARATION (human_control_availability)

Two people can review each other here, but nobody independent approves exceptions. **[HUMAN_CONTROL_NO_SEPARATION]**

- **Why it matters:** Exceptions lack separation of duties.
- **Fix:** Use an approver from platform or security for exceptions and uat/prod.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/ROLLOUT_PLAN.md](../adoption/ROLLOUT_PLAN.md)

### HUMAN_CONTROL_UNVALIDATED (human_control_availability)

A control needs a second person, and this repository has only one. **[HUMAN_CONTROL_UNVALIDATED]**

- **Why it matters:** The control cannot exist here; it is recorded as unvalidated.
- **Fix:** Name an approver from platform or security outside the team (docs/adoption/ROLLOUT_PLAN.md, small teams).
- **More:** [docs/adoption/ROLLOUT_PLAN.md](../adoption/ROLLOUT_PLAN.md)

## kit_api_refusal

### API_CORRELATION_MISMATCH (kit_api_refusal)

The correlation id in the dispatch and in the request differ. **[API_CORRELATION_MISMATCH]**

- **Why it matters:** The API refuses by name before doing anything, so nothing changed.
- **Fix:** Send the same id in both; let scripts/kit_api.py make it.
- **More:** [docs/api/README.md](../api/README.md)

### API_CREDENTIAL_ABSENT (kit_api_refusal)

The API client has no token. **[API_CREDENTIAL_ABSENT]**

- **Why it matters:** The API refuses by name before doing anything, so nothing changed.
- **Fix:** Set GH_TOKEN (or KIT_API_TOKEN), or KIT_API_AUTH=proxy behind a credential proxy.
- **More:** [docs/api/README.md](../api/README.md)

### API_DEPLOY_NEEDS_HUMAN_APPROVAL (kit_api_refusal)

The target environment does not require a human approver with self-review prevented. **[API_DEPLOY_NEEDS_HUMAN_APPROVAL]**

- **Why it matters:** The API refuses by name before doing anything, so nothing changed.
- **Fix:** Protect the environment with required reviewers and prevent self-review.
- **More:** [docs/api/README.md](../api/README.md)

### API_DISPOSITION_NOT_VIA_API (kit_api_refusal)

An exception, false positive or risk acceptance was requested through the API. **[API_DISPOSITION_NOT_VIA_API]**

- **Why it matters:** The API refuses by name before doing anything, so nothing changed.
- **Fix:** Open a pull request to the policy register; dispositions are merged under CODEOWNERS.
- **More:** [docs/api/README.md](../api/README.md)

### API_DUPLICATE_REQUEST (kit_api_refusal)

This idempotency key was already used; nothing was done again. **[API_DUPLICATE_REQUEST]**

- **Why it matters:** The API refuses by name before doing anything, so nothing changed.
- **Fix:** Read the first call's result with status.get.
- **More:** [docs/api/README.md](../api/README.md)

### API_ENVIRONMENT_NOT_PERMITTED (kit_api_refusal)

The environment is not in this repository's API deploy list, or a build was asked for uat/prod. **[API_ENVIRONMENT_NOT_PERMITTED]**

- **Why it matters:** The API refuses by name before doing anything, so nothing changed.
- **Fix:** Use a listed environment (vars.KIT_API_DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENTS); reach uat and prod by promotion.
- **More:** [docs/api/README.md](../api/README.md)

### API_EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE (kit_api_refusal)

The named security run is not a completed default-branch run, or its evidence has expired. **[API_EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE]**

- **Why it matters:** The API refuses by name before doing anything, so nothing changed.
- **Fix:** Name a completed default-branch run within the artifact retention.
- **More:** [docs/api/README.md](../api/README.md)

### API_FILTER_NEEDS_FINDINGS_RUN (kit_api_refusal)

A CVE, KEV or text filter needs a findings run id. **[API_FILTER_NEEDS_FINDINGS_RUN]**

- **Why it matters:** The API refuses by name before doing anything, so nothing changed.
- **Fix:** Add findings_run_id (or "latest").
- **More:** [docs/api/README.md](../api/README.md)

### API_FINDING_NOT_KIT_ESTABLISHED (kit_api_refusal)

A selected finding is not one the kit's scan established. **[API_FINDING_NOT_KIT_ESTABLISHED]**

- **Why it matters:** The API refuses by name before doing anything, so nothing changed.
- **Fix:** Select from that run's findings (findings.search).
- **More:** [docs/api/README.md](../api/README.md)

### API_HOST_INSECURE (kit_api_refusal)

The API address is not https. **[API_HOST_INSECURE]**

- **Why it matters:** The API refuses by name before doing anything, so nothing changed.
- **Fix:** Use the https API URL.
- **More:** [docs/api/README.md](../api/README.md)

### API_HOST_NOT_NAMED (kit_api_refusal)

The API client was not told which GitHub host to call. **[API_HOST_NOT_NAMED]**

- **Why it matters:** The API refuses by name before doing anything, so nothing changed.
- **Fix:** Set GH_HOST (for example <tenant>.ghe.com) or KIT_API_URL.
- **More:** [docs/api/README.md](../api/README.md)

### API_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED (kit_api_refusal)

A write request came without an idempotency key (or with two different ones). **[API_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED]**

- **Why it matters:** The API refuses by name before doing anything, so nothing changed.
- **Fix:** Send one key per intended write, the same in both places.
- **More:** [docs/api/README.md](../api/README.md)

### API_IDEMPOTENCY_UNVERIFIED (kit_api_refusal)

The kit could not check whether this key was used before, so it did not risk a write. **[API_IDEMPOTENCY_UNVERIFIED]**

- **Why it matters:** The API refuses by name before doing anything, so nothing changed.
- **Fix:** Retry with the same key.
- **More:** [docs/api/README.md](../api/README.md)

### API_OPERATION_NOT_ENABLED (kit_api_refusal)

This repository has not turned on the requested API operation. **[API_OPERATION_NOT_ENABLED]**

- **Why it matters:** The API refuses by name before doing anything, so nothing changed.
- **Fix:** The repository owner adds it to vars.KIT_API_OPERATIONS, or call another repository.
- **More:** [docs/api/README.md](../api/README.md)

### API_OPERATION_UNKNOWN (kit_api_refusal)

The API request names an operation that does not exist. **[API_OPERATION_UNKNOWN]**

- **Why it matters:** The API refuses by name before doing anything, so nothing changed.
- **Fix:** Use an operation listed in docs/api/README.md.
- **More:** [docs/api/README.md](../api/README.md)

### API_PROMOTION_SOURCE_REQUIRED (kit_api_refusal)

A promotion was requested without the run and environment to promote from. **[API_PROMOTION_SOURCE_REQUIRED]**

- **Why it matters:** The API refuses by name before doing anything, so nothing changed.
- **Fix:** Name promote_from_run_id and promote_from_environment.
- **More:** [docs/api/README.md](../api/README.md)

### API_REF_NOT_DEFAULT_BRANCH (kit_api_refusal)

A ticket or deploy call was dispatched on a branch other than the default branch. **[API_REF_NOT_DEFAULT_BRANCH]**

- **Why it matters:** The API refuses by name before doing anything, so nothing changed.
- **Fix:** Dispatch on the default branch.
- **More:** [docs/api/README.md](../api/README.md)

### API_RELEASE_PATH_NOT_PERMITTED (kit_api_refusal)

Rollback and break-glass cannot be requested through the API. **[API_RELEASE_PATH_NOT_PERMITTED]**

- **Why it matters:** The API refuses by name before doing anything, so nothing changed.
- **Fix:** A person dispatches the release workflow with the exception record.
- **More:** [docs/api/README.md](../api/README.md)

### API_REPOSITORY_NOT_SERVED (kit_api_refusal)

The request names another repository; each API instance serves only its own. **[API_REPOSITORY_NOT_SERVED]**

- **Why it matters:** The API refuses by name before doing anything, so nothing changed.
- **Fix:** Call that repository's kit-api.
- **More:** [docs/api/README.md](../api/README.md)

### API_REQUEST_TOO_LARGE (kit_api_refusal)

The API request is over 60,000 characters. **[API_REQUEST_TOO_LARGE]**

- **Why it matters:** The API refuses by name before doing anything, so nothing changed.
- **Fix:** Select fewer findings or page the search.
- **More:** [docs/api/README.md](../api/README.md)

### API_REQUEST_UNPARSEABLE (kit_api_refusal)

The API request is not a JSON object. **[API_REQUEST_UNPARSEABLE]**

- **Why it matters:** The API refuses by name before doing anything, so nothing changed.
- **Fix:** Send the envelope in api/v1/request.schema.json.
- **More:** [docs/api/README.md](../api/README.md)

### API_REVIEW_NOT_FINALIZED (kit_api_refusal)

The review behind the tickets is not finalized with a recorded second-person approval. **[API_REVIEW_NOT_FINALIZED]**

- **Why it matters:** The API refuses by name before doing anything, so nothing changed.
- **Fix:** Have the concurring reviewer approve and merge the review record.
- **More:** [docs/api/README.md](../api/README.md)

### API_SCHEMA_VIOLATION (kit_api_refusal)

A field in the API request is invalid. **[API_SCHEMA_VIOLATION]**

- **Why it matters:** The API refuses by name before doing anything, so nothing changed.
- **Fix:** Correct the field the refusal names.
- **More:** [docs/api/README.md](../api/README.md)

### API_TEMPLATE_INVALID (kit_api_refusal)

A ticket template item is invalid; data.template_refusal names the rule. **[API_TEMPLATE_INVALID]**

- **Why it matters:** The API refuses by name before doing anything, so nothing changed.
- **Fix:** Correct the named item; nothing was read or written.
- **More:** [docs/api/README.md](../api/README.md)

### API_TEMPLATE_RULE_REFUSED (kit_api_refusal)

A ticket rule that reads the tracker refused an item before anything was written. **[API_TEMPLATE_RULE_REFUSED]**

- **Why it matters:** The API refuses by name before doing anything, so nothing changed.
- **Fix:** Read data.template_refusal and correct the item.
- **More:** [docs/api/README.md](../api/README.md)

### API_TICKET_NOT_KIT_STAMPED (kit_api_refusal)

The ticket does not carry the kit's stamp, so the kit does not own it. **[API_TICKET_NOT_KIT_STAMPED]**

- **Why it matters:** The API refuses by name before doing anything, so nothing changed.
- **Fix:** Comment on it in the tracker directly.
- **More:** [docs/api/README.md](../api/README.md)

### API_TRACKER_QUERY_REFUSED (kit_api_refusal)

A tracker query named a project outside this repository's, or a forbidden clause. **[API_TRACKER_QUERY_REFUSED]**

- **Why it matters:** The API refuses by name before doing anything, so nothing changed.
- **Fix:** Query only this repository's projects, without ORDER BY.
- **More:** [docs/api/README.md](../api/README.md)

### API_TRANSPORT_NOT_PERMITTED (kit_api_refusal)

A release was requested by repository_dispatch, which the API does not accept for releases. **[API_TRANSPORT_NOT_PERMITTED]**

- **Why it matters:** The API refuses by name before doing anything, so nothing changed.
- **Fix:** Send it by workflow_dispatch.
- **More:** [docs/api/README.md](../api/README.md)

### API_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED (kit_api_refusal)

The API request names a version the kit does not serve. **[API_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED]**

- **Why it matters:** The API refuses by name before doing anything, so nothing changed.
- **Fix:** Send api_version v1.
- **More:** [docs/api/README.md](../api/README.md)

## kit_api_state

Not failures (nothing to do): `API_ACCEPTED`, `API_COMPLETED`, `API_IN_PROGRESS`, `API_QUEUED`.

### API_AWAITING_APPROVAL (kit_api_state)

The API call is waiting for a person to approve a release in its environment. **[API_AWAITING_APPROVAL]**

- **Why it matters:** The API never approves anything itself.
- **Fix:** A reviewer approves it in the run page (Review deployments).
- **More:** [docs/api/README.md](../api/README.md)

### API_CANCELLED (kit_api_state)

The API run was cancelled before it answered. **[API_CANCELLED]**

- **Why it matters:** Nothing is known about the outcome.
- **Fix:** Resubmit with the same idempotency key.
- **More:** [docs/api/README.md](../api/README.md)

### API_FAILED (kit_api_state)

The API call was accepted but could not be carried out. **[API_FAILED]**

- **Why it matters:** It is never a success.
- **Fix:** Read the result's reason (tracker unreachable, a release that did not report) and retry with the same idempotency key.
- **More:** [docs/api/README.md](../api/README.md)

### API_NOT_FOUND (kit_api_state)

No run for this API call has appeared yet. **[API_NOT_FOUND]**

- **Why it matters:** A dispatch can take seconds to appear; not found is not refused.
- **Fix:** Wait a few seconds and check the status again (status.get).
- **More:** [docs/api/README.md](../api/README.md)

### API_REFUSED (kit_api_state)

The API call was refused by name before anything was done. **[API_REFUSED]**

- **Why it matters:** The refusal (an API_ code) says exactly why.
- **Fix:** Read the refusal code; each has its own entry in this catalogue.
- **More:** [docs/api/README.md](../api/README.md)

### API_RESULT_UNREADABLE (kit_api_state)

The API run finished, but no valid result for this call could be read. **[API_RESULT_UNREADABLE]**

- **Why it matters:** A finished run is not a finished call.
- **Fix:** Read the run's log and summary; retry with the same idempotency key.
- **More:** [docs/api/README.md](../api/README.md)

## kit_init_state

Not failures (nothing to do): `KIT_INIT_PR_OPENED`, `KIT_INIT_UNCHANGED`, `KIT_INIT_WRITTEN`.

### KIT_INIT_API_NEEDS_CONTAINER (kit_init_state)

The kit API caller was requested, but this repository is not a container deploy. **[KIT_INIT_API_NEEDS_CONTAINER]**

- **Why it matters:** The API's release path calls build-deploy.yml, which exists only for container deploys.
- **Fix:** Drop --with-api for now (scans and findings need no API).
- **More:** [docs/adoption/GETTING_STARTED_1_HOUR.md](../adoption/GETTING_STARTED_1_HOUR.md)

### KIT_INIT_DIRTY_TREE (kit_init_state)

The repository has uncommitted changes, so kit init did not open its pull request. **[KIT_INIT_DIRTY_TREE]**

- **Why it matters:** It commits only its own files, from a clean tree.
- **Fix:** Commit or stash your changes and run again, or use --dry-run to write files only.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/GETTING_STARTED_1_HOUR.md](../adoption/GETTING_STARTED_1_HOUR.md)

### KIT_INIT_GENERATED_INVALID (kit_init_state)

kit init's own check of the files it generated failed, so it wrote nothing. **[KIT_INIT_GENERATED_INVALID]**

- **Why it matters:** This is a kit defect, not a problem with your repository.
- **Fix:** Send the output to the platform team; pin a different kit commit meanwhile.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/GETTING_STARTED_1_HOUR.md](../adoption/GETTING_STARTED_1_HOUR.md)

### KIT_INIT_HOST_UNSUPPORTED (kit_init_state)

The repository's host is neither github.com nor a <tenant>.ghe.com host. **[KIT_INIT_HOST_UNSUPPORTED]**

- **Why it matters:** The kit supports only those two hosts.
- **Fix:** Pass --host github.com or --host <tenant>.ghe.com.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/GETTING_STARTED_1_HOUR.md](../adoption/GETTING_STARTED_1_HOUR.md)

### KIT_INIT_HUMAN_EDIT_PRESERVED (kit_init_state)

kit init kept a file (or the CODEOWNERS block) exactly as a person left it, instead of updating it. **[KIT_INIT_HUMAN_EDIT_PRESERVED]**

- **Why it matters:** A person's edit always wins; that file did not get the kit's newest version.
- **Fix:** Nothing, if your edit is intended. To take the kit's version, delete the file (or the block's marker lines) and run kit init again.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/GETTING_STARTED_1_HOUR.md](../adoption/GETTING_STARTED_1_HOUR.md)

### KIT_INIT_MULTIPLE_IMAGES (kit_init_state)

This repository has more than one Dockerfile and kit init will not pick which one deploys. **[KIT_INIT_MULTIPLE_IMAGES]**

- **Why it matters:** Picking the wrong image would deploy the wrong thing.
- **Fix:** Re-run with --dockerfile path/to/Dockerfile (in the workflow: re-run kit init locally with that flag).
- **More:** [docs/adoption/GETTING_STARTED_1_HOUR.md](../adoption/GETTING_STARTED_1_HOUR.md)

### KIT_INIT_PIN_MISSING (kit_init_state)

kit init was not told which kit repository and commit to pin. **[KIT_INIT_PIN_MISSING]**

- **Why it matters:** Every kit reference must be pinned to one exact commit.
- **Fix:** Pass --kit-repo OWNER/REPO and --kit-sha <40-hex commit>; the workflow wrapper takes both from its own uses: line.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/GETTING_STARTED_1_HOUR.md](../adoption/GETTING_STARTED_1_HOUR.md)

### KIT_INIT_PIN_NOT_CHECKOUT (kit_init_state)

The commit you asked kit init to pin is not the kit commit it is running from. **[KIT_INIT_PIN_NOT_CHECKOUT]**

- **Why it matters:** The files would describe one kit version and pin another.
- **Fix:** Check out the kit at the commit you want (git checkout <sha>) and run again, or omit --kit-sha.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/GETTING_STARTED_1_HOUR.md](../adoption/GETTING_STARTED_1_HOUR.md)

### KIT_INIT_PR_NOT_OPENED (kit_init_state)

kit init wrote the files but git or gh refused to push the branch or open the pull request. **[KIT_INIT_PR_NOT_OPENED]**

- **Why it matters:** Nothing was lost; the files are in your working tree.
- **Fix:** Check the token can push (Contents, Pull requests and Workflows: write) and GH_HOST is your host; then commit and open the PR yourself.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/GETTING_STARTED_1_HOUR.md](../adoption/GETTING_STARTED_1_HOUR.md)

### KIT_INIT_SECRET_REFUSED (kit_init_state)

kit init found a secret-looking value in what it was about to write, so it wrote nothing. **[KIT_INIT_SECRET_REFUSED]**

- **Why it matters:** Generated files are committed; a secret in them would leak.
- **Fix:** Remove the secret from the path or variable the message names (and rotate it), then run again.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/GETTING_STARTED_1_HOUR.md](../adoption/GETTING_STARTED_1_HOUR.md)

### KIT_INIT_STACK_UNKNOWN (kit_init_state)

kit init did not recognise any language or deploy type in this repository, so it wrote nothing. **[KIT_INIT_STACK_UNKNOWN]**

- **Why it matters:** It never guesses a pipeline: a wrong one would scan the wrong things and look green.
- **Fix:** Add the missing manifest (requirements.txt, package.json, pom.xml, go.mod, a .csproj, composer.json, a Dockerfile, *.tf or *.bicep), or copy templates/security.yml by hand.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/GETTING_STARTED_1_HOUR.md](../adoption/GETTING_STARTED_1_HOUR.md)

## kit_watermark

Not failures (nothing to do): `WATERMARK_ABSENT`, `WATERMARK_BOUND`.

### WATERMARK_DIRTY (kit_watermark)

The kit copy you call was exported from uncommitted changes. **[WATERMARK_DIRTY]**

- **Why it matters:** Nobody can say exactly which kit code ran.
- **Fix:** Ask the platform team to re-export the kit from a clean commit and repin.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### WATERMARK_UNREADABLE (kit_watermark)

The kit copy you call has a damaged version marker. **[WATERMARK_UNREADABLE]**

- **Why it matters:** Nobody can tie the pinned SHA to the kit source.
- **Fix:** Ask the platform team to re-export the kit.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

## known_exploited

Not failures (nothing to do): `AVAILABLE`, `CLEAR`.

### EXCEPTED (known_exploited)

A dependency has a known-exploited vulnerability that an approved, ticketed exception covers for now. **[EXCEPTED]**

- **Why it matters:** It is not clean: attackers use this vulnerability; a named person accepted it until a date.
- **Fix:** Upgrade the dependency to a fixed version before the exception expires.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### FINDING_KNOWN_EXPLOITED (known_exploited)
