A dependency or image contains a vulnerability that attackers are actively exploiting (it is on the CISA KEV list). **[FINDING_KNOWN_EXPLOITED]**

- **Why it matters:** This always blocks, at every enforcement level: it is the kind of flaw used in real attacks today.
- **Fix:** Upgrade the package to the fixed version the finding names (Dependabot may already have a pull request), then push.
- **More:** [docs/security-review/READING-THE-RUN-SUMMARY.md](../security-review/READING-THE-RUN-SUMMARY.md)

### UNAVAILABLE (known_exploited)

The known-exploited vulnerability check could not run: the catalog could not be fetched or read. **[UNAVAILABLE]**

- **Why it matters:** Nobody confirmed your dependencies are free of actively exploited vulnerabilities on this run.
- **Fix:** Re-run later; if it persists, the platform team checks the network path to the catalog or the feed mirror.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/FEED_MIRRORS.md](../adoption/FEED_MIRRORS.md)

## known_exploited_exception_refusal

### EXCEPTION_HISTORY_TAMPERED (known_exploited_exception_refusal)

Same meaning and fix as [`policy_resolution.EXCEPTION_HISTORY_TAMPERED`](#exception_history_tampered-policy_resolution).

### EXCEPTION_HISTORY_UNVERIFIED (known_exploited_exception_refusal)

Same meaning and fix as [`policy_resolution.EXCEPTION_HISTORY_UNVERIFIED`](#exception_history_unverified-policy_resolution).

### EXCEPTION_RENEWAL_LIMIT (known_exploited_exception_refusal)

Same meaning and fix as [`policy_resolution.EXCEPTION_RENEWAL_LIMIT`](#exception_renewal_limit-policy_resolution).

### KEV_EXCEPTION_EXPIRED (known_exploited_exception_refusal)

A known-exploited exception has passed its expiry date. **[KEV_EXCEPTION_EXPIRED]**

- **Why it matters:** The vulnerability blocks again.
- **Fix:** Upgrade the dependency, or ask the approver for a new expiry.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### KEV_EXCEPTION_NOT_FINDING_SCOPED (known_exploited_exception_refusal)

A known-exploited exception does not name exactly one finding and one CVE. **[KEV_EXCEPTION_NOT_FINDING_SCOPED]**

- **Why it matters:** A blanket exception is never accepted; the vulnerability still blocks.
- **Fix:** Name the finding fingerprint and the CVE in the exception.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### KEV_EXCEPTION_UNATTRIBUTED (known_exploited_exception_refusal)

A known-exploited exception is missing its explanation, approver, expiry or reviewers, or its history cannot be read. **[KEV_EXCEPTION_UNATTRIBUTED]**

- **Why it matters:** An unexplained exception is refused; the vulnerability still blocks.
- **Fix:** Fill in the missing fields the summary names.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### KEV_EXCEPTION_UNTICKETED (known_exploited_exception_refusal)

A known-exploited exception has no valid work-item ticket. **[KEV_EXCEPTION_UNTICKETED]**

- **Why it matters:** Every exception must be traceable; the vulnerability still blocks.
- **Fix:** Add the ticket key (PROJECT-1234) to the exception.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

## leak_gate_setup_refusal

### BASELINE_UNREADABLE (leak_gate_setup_refusal)

The kit's baseline .gitignore next to the helper is missing or empty. **[BASELINE_UNREADABLE]**

- **Why it matters:** There is nothing to merge; the kit copy is damaged.
- **Fix:** Re-fetch the kit at its pinned SHA and run again.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/LEAK_GATES.md](../adoption/LEAK_GATES.md)

### MERGE_NOT_VERIFIED (leak_gate_setup_refusal)

After writing .gitignore, at least one baseline pattern is still missing. **[MERGE_NOT_VERIFIED]**

- **Why it matters:** Success is claimed only for what the file really contains.
- **Fix:** Re-run merge-baseline.sh; it names each missing pattern on stderr.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/LEAK_GATES.md](../adoption/LEAK_GATES.md)

### NOT_APPLIED (leak_gate_setup_refusal)

GitHub refused to create the push ruleset (no admin rights, or the plan does not support rulesets). **[NOT_APPLIED]**

- **Why it matters:** The layer is not in place.
- **Fix:** Run apply-push-ruleset.sh as a repository admin; on a personal or unlicensed repository, rulesets are not available.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/LEAK_GATES.md](../adoption/LEAK_GATES.md)

### NOT_A_GIT_REPO (leak_gate_setup_refusal)

The directory given to merge-baseline.sh is not a git repository. **[NOT_A_GIT_REPO]**

- **Why it matters:** A .gitignore outside a repository protects nothing.
- **Fix:** Pass the root folder of a git clone.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/LEAK_GATES.md](../adoption/LEAK_GATES.md)

### REPO_DIR_MISSING (leak_gate_setup_refusal)

The directory given to merge-baseline.sh does not exist. **[REPO_DIR_MISSING]**

- **Why it matters:** Nothing was written.
- **Fix:** Pass the path of your repository's root folder.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/LEAK_GATES.md](../adoption/LEAK_GATES.md)

### REPO_NOT_READABLE (leak_gate_setup_refusal)

The ruleset helper could not read the repository (wrong name, wrong host, or no access). **[REPO_NOT_READABLE]**

- **Why it matters:** Nothing was attempted.
- **Fix:** Check OWNER/REPO and GH_HOST (a <tenant>.ghe.com repository needs GH_HOST set), and that your token can read it.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/LEAK_GATES.md](../adoption/LEAK_GATES.md)

### RULESET_LOOKUP_FAILED (leak_gate_setup_refusal)

The helper could not list the repository's rulesets, so it does not know whether the kit's ruleset exists. **[RULESET_LOOKUP_FAILED]**

- **Why it matters:** Creating one blindly could duplicate it; nothing was done.
- **Fix:** Re-run with a token that can read rulesets (repository administration read).
- **More:** [docs/adoption/LEAK_GATES.md](../adoption/LEAK_GATES.md)

### TARGET_NOT_WRITABLE (leak_gate_setup_refusal)

The repository's .gitignore could not be written. **[TARGET_NOT_WRITABLE]**

- **Why it matters:** The baseline patterns are not (all) in place.
- **Fix:** Make .gitignore writable (check its permissions or a lock) and re-run; the merge completes without duplicates.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/LEAK_GATES.md](../adoption/LEAK_GATES.md)

### TEMPLATE_UNREADABLE (leak_gate_setup_refusal)

The kit's push-ruleset file next to the helper is missing or broken. **[TEMPLATE_UNREADABLE]**

- **Why it matters:** There is nothing to apply; the kit copy is damaged.
- **Fix:** Re-fetch the kit at its pinned SHA and run again.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/LEAK_GATES.md](../adoption/LEAK_GATES.md)

## leak_gate_state

Not failures (nothing to do): `ON`.

### NO_LEAK_GATE_SHOWN (leak_gate_state)

Only the CI secret scan stands between a committed secret and main: no other protection could be shown on. **[NO_LEAK_GATE_SHOWN]**

- **Why it matters:** A secret is caught only after it is already pushed.
- **Fix:** Turn on push protection or apply the kit's push ruleset (docs/adoption/LEAK_GATES.md steps 1-3).
- **More:** [docs/adoption/LEAK_GATES.md](../adoption/LEAK_GATES.md)

### OFF (leak_gate_state)

One of the layers that stop a committed secret reaching main is switched off. **[OFF]**

- **Why it matters:** Secrets get one fewer chance to be caught before they land.
- **Fix:** Turn the named layer on (push protection or the push ruleset); docs/adoption/LEAK_GATES.md has the exact steps.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/LEAK_GATES.md](../adoption/LEAK_GATES.md)

### UNKNOWN (leak_gate_state)

The kit could not read whether a secret-protection layer is on (this token cannot see it). **[UNKNOWN]**

- **Why it matters:** Unknown is neither on nor off; nobody knows.
- **Fix:** Ask a repository admin to confirm the layer in Settings > Code security, or grant the read the summary names.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/LEAK_GATES.md](../adoption/LEAK_GATES.md)

## oidc_subject_form

Not failures (nothing to do): `ID_QUALIFIED`, `PLAIN`.

### UNMATCHED (oidc_subject_form)

The identity GitHub presented does not match the federated credential's expected subject. **[UNMATCHED]**

- **Why it matters:** Azure will refuse the sign-in (AADSTS700213); nothing was attempted.
- **Fix:** Add a federated credential whose subject is exactly repo:<org>/<repo>:environment:<env> (case-sensitive), with this host's issuer.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/SETUP.md](../adoption/SETUP.md)

## platform_applicability

Not failures (nothing to do): `APPLICABLE`, `NOT_APPLICABLE`.

### NOT_CONFIGURED (platform_applicability)

A check is available but switched off for this repository. **[NOT_CONFIGURED]**

- **Why it matters:** It did not run; someone chose that, or never chose.
- **Fix:** Ask a repository admin whether it should be on (the summary names the setting).
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### UNAVAILABLE (platform_applicability)

A check is not available to this repository (not licensed, or the feature is off for the organisation). **[UNAVAILABLE]**

- **Why it matters:** That check could not run; it is a platform decision, not something your code did.
- **Fix:** Nothing for you; the platform team decides whether to license or replace it (on GHE.com with GHAS off, CodeQL is not graded).
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### UNKNOWN (platform_applicability)

The kit could not tell whether a check applies here (the token could not see the setting). **[UNKNOWN]**

- **Why it matters:** The check runs anyway, and the result says so.
- **Fix:** Nothing for you; an admin can confirm the setting.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

## policy_notice

### ORG_UNMAPPED_RAN_AT_ENTERPRISE_FLOOR (policy_notice)

This organisation is not named in the central policy, so the run used the enterprise minimum. **[ORG_UNMAPPED_RAN_AT_ENTERPRISE_FLOOR]**

- **Why it matters:** You are checked at the safe floor; your organisation's own policy was not applied.
- **Fix:** Ask the policy owner to add this organisation to the central register's orgs map.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### ORG_UNMAPPED_RAN_AT_STRICTEST_ORG (policy_notice)

This organisation is not known to the central policy, so the run used the strictest registered organisation's rules. **[ORG_UNMAPPED_RAN_AT_STRICTEST_ORG]**

- **Why it matters:** You are checked strictly until someone registers your organisation.
- **Fix:** Ask the policy owner to register this organisation in the central register.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

## policy_resolution

Not failures (nothing to do): `POLICY_RESOLVED`, `RUNG_EFFECTIVE_BELOW_DECLARED`.

### CELLS_NOT_MONOTONE (policy_resolution)

The policy makes a lower environment stricter than a higher one (for example dev stricter than prod). **[CELLS_NOT_MONOTONE]**

- **Why it matters:** Enforcement must grow along the promotion path, or problems are found weeks later at the last gate.
- **Fix:** Ask the policy owner to order the rungs so dev <= test <= uat = prod.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### CELL_NOT_REGISTERED (policy_resolution)

The policy file has no entry for the environment this run is checked for. **[CELL_NOT_REGISTERED]**

- **Why it matters:** Without an entry there is no floor to apply, so the result cannot be trusted.
- **Fix:** Add an entry for the environment the summary names, or map the environment name to a tier in environment_names.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### CHERRY_PICK_BELOW_FLOOR (policy_resolution)

The policy (or a workflow input) asks for less than the kit's minimum: a secret check below blocking, or a required scan switched off. **[CHERRY_PICK_BELOW_FLOOR]**

- **Why it matters:** Secret, known-exploited and malicious-package checks always block; nobody can switch them off.
- **Fix:** Remove the setting the summary names (for example enable_malicious_pkg_scan: false) from the policy or the workflow.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### EXCEPTION_HISTORY_TAMPERED (policy_resolution)

An exception claims fewer renewals than the git history of the policy file shows. **[EXCEPTION_HISTORY_TAMPERED]**

- **Why it matters:** The recorded history must match what actually happened; the exception is refused and the run blocks.
- **Fix:** Correct the exception's renewal history to match git (the summary shows the count) and have it re-approved.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### EXCEPTION_HISTORY_UNVERIFIED (policy_resolution)

The kit could not read the git history of the policy file, so it cannot check how often an exception was renewed. **[EXCEPTION_HISTORY_UNVERIFIED]**

- **Why it matters:** An unreadable history is never treated as zero renewals; the exception does not apply.
- **Fix:** Check out with full history (actions/checkout fetch-depth: 0) or ask the platform team; then re-run.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### EXCEPTION_RENEWAL_LIMIT (policy_resolution)

An exception has been renewed more times than the policy allows. **[EXCEPTION_RENEWAL_LIMIT]**

- **Why it matters:** Endless renewals hide a problem; the exception is refused and the finding is treated normally again.
- **Fix:** Fix the underlying finding; a further exception needs the policy owner to decide, not another renewal.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### ORG_NOT_UNDER_ENTERPRISE (policy_resolution)

This refusal is retired and no longer emitted. **[ORG_NOT_UNDER_ENTERPRISE]**

- **Why it matters:** It is kept only because older records name it.
- **Fix:** Nothing to do; if you see it, the kit version is old: update the pinned kit SHA.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### POLICY_BELOW_AUTHORITY_FLOOR (policy_resolution)

A policy entry for a narrower scope (team, product, repository) tries to go below what a broader scope set. **[POLICY_BELOW_AUTHORITY_FLOOR]**

- **Why it matters:** Narrower scopes may only tighten; the floor holds and the run blocks.
- **Fix:** Ask the policy owner to raise the entry to at least the floor the summary names.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### POLICY_DECISION_EXPIRED (policy_resolution)

A policy entry that applies to this run has passed its expiry date. **[POLICY_DECISION_EXPIRED]**

- **Why it matters:** Any loosening it gave is withdrawn until someone renews or replaces it.
- **Fix:** Ask the policy owner to renew the entry (new expires date) or remove it.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### POLICY_DECISION_UNATTRIBUTED (policy_resolution)

A policy entry has no recorded owner, reason, decision date or expiry. **[POLICY_DECISION_UNATTRIBUTED]**

- **Why it matters:** Every policy is a decision by a named person; an unsigned one is refused.
- **Fix:** Ask the policy owner to add the decision fields (authority, reason, decided_on, expires) to the entry the summary names.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### POLICY_MODE_SUPPLIED (policy_resolution)

The workflow passed a policy mode as an input; the kit derives it and never accepts it from a caller. **[POLICY_MODE_SUPPLIED]**

- **Why it matters:** A derived value that a caller can override is not a control.
- **Fix:** Remove the policy_mode input from your workflow; set enforcement through the policy register instead.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### POLICY_NUMBER_NOT_CONFIGURED (policy_resolution)

A number the policy needs (a count, a period, a grace time) is missing from the policy file. **[POLICY_NUMBER_NOT_CONFIGURED]**

- **Why it matters:** The kit never invents a number on the owner's behalf.
- **Fix:** Ask the policy owner to add the number the summary names to the register's numbers block.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### POLICY_REGISTER_CONFLICT (policy_resolution)

Two policy entries disagree about the same thing, so the kit cannot tell which one applies. **[POLICY_REGISTER_CONFLICT]**

- **Why it matters:** Picking one by file order would be an accident, not a decision.
- **Fix:** Ask the policy owner to remove one of the two entries the summary names (in .security/policy-registration.json or the central register).
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### REGISTRATION_UNAVAILABLE (policy_resolution)

The policy file could not be read (invalid JSON, wrong schema, or the protected branch could not be reached). **[REGISTRATION_UNAVAILABLE]**

- **Why it matters:** An unreadable policy is not the default policy; the run cannot decide.
- **Fix:** Validate .security/policy-registration.json against the schema (python3 scripts/policy_registration.py --validate .security/policy-registration.json --origin repository) and fix the error it names.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### REPOSITORY_FILE_SOFTENING (policy_resolution)

This repository's own policy file tries to make a check weaker than the organisation's policy allows. **[REPOSITORY_FILE_SOFTENING]**

- **Why it matters:** A repository may make its policy stricter, never looser; the loosening is ignored and the run blocks.
- **Fix:** Remove the loosening from .security/policy-registration.json, or ask the central policy owner for the change.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### TICKET_ROUTING_BELOW_FLOOR (policy_resolution)

A policy entry routes secrets, known-exploited or malicious-package findings to "no ticket". **[TICKET_ROUTING_BELOW_FLOOR]**

- **Why it matters:** Those findings must always be ticketed somewhere; switching them off is refused.
- **Fix:** Route them to a real project in the policy entry the summary names.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

## prerequisite_readiness

Not failures (nothing to do): `ACQUIRED_AND_READY`, `READY`.

### ACQUISITION_UNAVAILABLE (prerequisite_readiness)

The kit tried to install a tool a check needs and could not. **[ACQUISITION_UNAVAILABLE]**

- **Why it matters:** The check cannot run.
- **Fix:** Re-run; if it persists, check the runner's network access to the tool's download site.
- **More:** [docs/operations/FAILURE_MODES.md](../operations/FAILURE_MODES.md)

### FITNESS_FAILED (prerequisite_readiness)

A tool is installed but does not work (it failed its self-check). **[FITNESS_FAILED]**

- **Why it matters:** A broken tool would give a meaningless result, so the check does not run.
- **Fix:** Re-run on a fresh runner; if it persists, report the tool and version in the log to the platform team.
- **More:** [docs/operations/FAILURE_MODES.md](../operations/FAILURE_MODES.md)

### PREREQUISITE_UNAVAILABLE (prerequisite_readiness)

A tool a check needs is missing on this runner, and the kit has no way to install it. **[PREREQUISITE_UNAVAILABLE]**

- **Why it matters:** The check cannot run here.
- **Fix:** Run on a GitHub-hosted runner (ubuntu-latest) or ask the platform team to add the tool to your runner.
- **More:** [docs/operations/FAILURE_MODES.md](../operations/FAILURE_MODES.md)

### REMEDIATION_FAILED (prerequisite_readiness)

The kit installed a missing tool, but it still does not work. **[REMEDIATION_FAILED]**

- **Why it matters:** The check cannot run.
- **Fix:** Send the job log to the platform team.
- **More:** [docs/operations/FAILURE_MODES.md](../operations/FAILURE_MODES.md)

## previous_state

Not failures (nothing to do): `EMPTY`, `EXISTING_DEPLOYMENT`.

### UNKNOWN (previous_state)

The deploy could not read what was running before it, so it did not change anything. **[UNKNOWN]**

- **Why it matters:** Without a known starting point, a safe rollback is impossible.
- **Fix:** Re-run; if it repeats, check the deploy identity can read the target (Reader on its resource group).
- **More:** [docs/adoption/SETUP.md](../adoption/SETUP.md)

## promotion_check

Not failures (nothing to do): `DAST_PASSED`, `NOT_APPLICABLE_PASSIVE`, `POSTURE_PASSED`.

### DAST_BLOCKING_FINDINGS (promotion_check)

The attack test (DAST) found an error-level issue in the running app. **[DAST_BLOCKING_FINDINGS]**

- **Why it matters:** The build is not marked tested, so it cannot be promoted.
- **Fix:** Read the DAST SARIF in the deploy evidence, fix the issue, redeploy.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### DAST_INCOMPLETE (promotion_check)

The attack test (DAST) left no readable report. **[DAST_INCOMPLETE]**

- **Why it matters:** An unfinished test is never a pass.
- **Fix:** Check KIT_DAST_COMMAND writes SARIF to $PROMOTION_DAST_SARIF and finishes within 30 minutes.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### POSTURE_FAILED (promotion_check)

A security setting on the running app does not hold (the summary names it). **[POSTURE_FAILED]**

- **Why it matters:** The app is live with a weaker setting than required.
- **Fix:** Fix the named setting (for example HTTPS only, minimum TLS) in your infrastructure code and redeploy.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### POSTURE_UNREADABLE (promotion_check)

The deploy could not read the running app's security settings. **[POSTURE_UNREADABLE]**

- **Why it matters:** An unreadable setting is not a passing one.
- **Fix:** Check the deploy identity can read the target (Reader); re-run.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/SETUP.md](../adoption/SETUP.md)

## promotion_gate

Not failures (nothing to do): `PREFLIGHT_PASSED`, `PROMOTION_ALLOWED`.

### BREAK_GLASS_REFUSED_EXPIRED (promotion_gate)

The break-glass exception's expiry date has passed. **[BREAK_GLASS_REFUSED_EXPIRED]**

- **Why it matters:** An expired emergency approval is not an approval.
- **Fix:** Get a new exception with a future expiry (at most 7 days).
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### BREAK_GLASS_REFUSED_NO_EXCEPTION (promotion_gate)

An emergency (break-glass) release was requested without a reason, authority, ticket and expiry. **[BREAK_GLASS_REFUSED_NO_EXCEPTION]**

- **Why it matters:** Break-glass is allowed only with a full exception record.
- **Fix:** Fill exception_reason, exception_authority, exception_approver, exception_ref and exception_expires.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### BREAK_GLASS_REFUSED_TOO_LONG (promotion_gate)

The break-glass exception expires more than 7 days out. **[BREAK_GLASS_REFUSED_TOO_LONG]**

- **Why it matters:** Emergency exceptions are short by rule.
- **Fix:** Set exception_expires within 7 days.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### DAST_REFUSED_PRODUCTION_TARGET (promotion_gate)

Active DAST (attack testing) was configured against prod. **[DAST_REFUSED_PRODUCTION_TARGET]**

- **Why it matters:** DAST runs against the environment before prod, never prod itself.
- **Fix:** Leave dast_command empty for prod (the template already does).
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### PROMOTION_REFUSED_DIGEST_MISMATCH (promotion_gate)

The image you are promoting is not the one the earlier environment verified. **[PROMOTION_REFUSED_DIGEST_MISMATCH]**

- **Why it matters:** Promotion must move the exact same bytes; a substitute is refused.
- **Fix:** Promote by run id with the template's promote job (it reads the digest from the record); do not type a digest.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### PROMOTION_REFUSED_NEW_FINDING (promotion_gate)

A fresh scan of the build found a high-severity issue that was not there at build time. **[PROMOTION_REFUSED_NEW_FINDING]**

- **Why it matters:** New vulnerabilities are published daily; the build is no longer what was approved.
- **Fix:** Upgrade the affected package, rebuild, test, and promote the new run.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### PROMOTION_REFUSED_NOT_FROM_MAIN (promotion_gate)

The build you are promoting was not built from the default branch. **[PROMOTION_REFUSED_NOT_FROM_MAIN]**

- **Why it matters:** Only merged, reviewed code reaches uat and prod.
- **Fix:** Merge your change to main, let it deploy to test, and promote that run.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### PROMOTION_REFUSED_NOT_VERIFIED (promotion_gate)

The earlier deploy did not pass everything needed to be promoted (health, e2e tests, posture). **[PROMOTION_REFUSED_NOT_VERIFIED]**

- **Why it matters:** Only a fully tested build moves on; the summary names what was missing.
- **Fix:** Fix what the record lists as missing (often KIT_E2E_TEST_COMMAND is unset), redeploy to test, then promote that run.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### PROMOTION_REFUSED_NO_PREDECESSOR (promotion_gate)

A uat or prod deploy named no run to promote from. **[PROMOTION_REFUSED_NO_PREDECESSOR]**

- **Why it matters:** uat and prod are only promoted, never built for.
- **Fix:** Dispatch the workflow with promote_from_run_id (the test deploy run) and promote_from_environment.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### PROMOTION_REFUSED_PATH_UNKNOWN (promotion_gate)

release_path is not one of normal, hotfix, rollback or break-glass. **[PROMOTION_REFUSED_PATH_UNKNOWN]**

- **Why it matters:** The deploy cannot pick rules for an unknown path.
- **Fix:** Set release_path to normal (or hotfix, rollback, break-glass with an exception record).
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### PROMOTION_REFUSED_RECHECK_INCOMPLETE (promotion_gate)

The re-check at promotion could not finish (SBOM scan, KEV list, history or revocations unreadable). **[PROMOTION_REFUSED_RECHECK_INCOMPLETE]**

- **Why it matters:** An unfinished check is not a pass.
- **Fix:** Re-run the promotion; if it persists, check the source run's artifacts still exist.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### PROMOTION_REFUSED_REVOKED (promotion_gate)

This build was revoked (listed in the revocation register, or a new critical or known-exploited issue was found). **[PROMOTION_REFUSED_REVOKED]**

- **Why it matters:** A revoked build is never promoted.
- **Fix:** Build and test a fixed version; the summary names the revocation reason.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### PROMOTION_REFUSED_SIGNATURE (promotion_gate)

The image's signed build record did not verify during promotion. **[PROMOTION_REFUSED_SIGNATURE]**

- **Why it matters:** Production gets only images whose origin is proven.
- **Fix:** Rebuild through the kit's build workflow from main; see the attestation entries in this catalogue.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/PROVENANCE_AND_ATTESTATION.md](../architecture/PROVENANCE_AND_ATTESTATION.md)

### PROMOTION_REFUSED_SOURCE_UNREADABLE (promotion_gate)

The run you promoted from has no readable promotion record for that environment. **[PROMOTION_REFUSED_SOURCE_UNREADABLE]**

- **Why it matters:** Without the record nobody can show the build was tested there.
- **Fix:** Check promote_from_run_id and promote_from_environment name a successful test (or uat) deploy run.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### PROMOTION_REFUSED_STALE (promotion_gate)

The build was verified more than 14 days ago. **[PROMOTION_REFUSED_STALE]**

- **Why it matters:** Old builds miss newer fixes and findings.
- **Fix:** Deploy a fresh build to test and promote that one (or record a rollback/hotfix decision).
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### PROMOTION_REFUSED_SUPERSEDED (promotion_gate)

A newer build has been verified in the same environment since this one. **[PROMOTION_REFUSED_SUPERSEDED]**

- **Why it matters:** Promoting an older build would skip the newer one.
- **Fix:** Promote the newest verified run instead.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### PROMOTION_REFUSED_WRONG_PREDECESSOR (promotion_gate)

The run you promoted from deployed to the wrong environment (for example dev instead of test). **[PROMOTION_REFUSED_WRONG_PREDECESSOR]**

- **Why it matters:** uat and prod accept only builds verified in their predecessor.
- **Fix:** Promote from the test deploy (or uat for prod, if your policy says so).
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### TEST_PERIOD_REFUSED_OUT_OF_BOUNDS (promotion_gate)

The end-to-end test period is not between 1 and 240 minutes. **[TEST_PERIOD_REFUSED_OUT_OF_BOUNDS]**

- **Why it matters:** A test period must be real and bounded.
- **Fix:** Set e2e_test_period_minutes to a value from 1 to 240.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

## promotion_revocation

### APPROVAL_REVOKED (promotion_revocation)

An approval behind the earlier deploy was revoked. **[APPROVAL_REVOKED]**

- **Why it matters:** The release lost its approval.
- **Fix:** Redeploy to the predecessor with a fresh approval, then promote.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### DIGEST_REVOKED (promotion_revocation)

This exact image is on the revocation list. **[DIGEST_REVOKED]**

- **Why it matters:** A revoked image is never promoted.
- **Fix:** Build, test and promote a new version.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### NEW_CRITICAL_FINDING (promotion_revocation)

A fresh scan found a critical vulnerability the build did not have before. **[NEW_CRITICAL_FINDING]**

- **Why it matters:** A critical issue blocks promotion.
- **Fix:** Upgrade the package, rebuild and promote the new run.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### NEW_KNOWN_EXPLOITED (promotion_revocation)

A package in this build is now on the known-exploited vulnerability list. **[NEW_KNOWN_EXPLOITED]**

- **Why it matters:** It blocks at every level.
- **Fix:** Upgrade the package, rebuild and promote the new run.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### SIGNING_IDENTITY_REVOKED (promotion_revocation)

The build workflow that signed this image has been revoked. **[SIGNING_IDENTITY_REVOKED]**

- **Why it matters:** Nothing it signed is trusted any more.
- **Fix:** Rebuild with the current kit build workflow and promote the new run.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### TEST_EVIDENCE_INVALIDATED (promotion_revocation)

The test results behind this build were declared invalid. **[TEST_EVIDENCE_INVALIDATED]**

- **Why it matters:** Untested builds are not promoted.
- **Fix:** Re-run the tests by redeploying to test, then promote that run.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

## publication_state

Not failures (nothing to do): `ANALYSIS_COMPLETE`, `PERSISTED`, `REPORT_PRODUCED`, `REPORT_STRUCTURALLY_VALID`.

### NO_FINDINGS_COUNT (publication_state)

The report job finished but published no count of blocking findings. **[NO_FINDINGS_COUNT]**

- **Why it matters:** No count is not a count of zero; the run cannot pass.
- **Fix:** Re-run; if it repeats, send the report job's log to the platform team.
- **More:** [docs/operations/FAILURE_MODES.md](../operations/FAILURE_MODES.md)

### PUBLICATION_DEGRADED (publication_state)

A place results are shown (such as the Security tab) was not available, so results were not published there. **[PUBLICATION_DEGRADED]**

- **Why it matters:** The scan itself still counts; only the display is missing. An empty Security tab is not a clean codebase.
- **Fix:** Read the results in the run summary and the evidence artifact instead.
- **More:** [docs/security-review/READING-THE-RUN-SUMMARY.md](../security-review/READING-THE-RUN-SUMMARY.md)

## readiness_source

Not failures (nothing to do): `READINESS_SOURCE_APPSEC_ATTESTATION`, `READINESS_SOURCE_LZ_HANDOFF`.

### READINESS_ATTESTATION_REFUSED (readiness_source)

The readiness attestation file exists, but one of its checks failed (expired, wrong environment, or not approved by AppSec). **[READINESS_ATTESTATION_REFUSED]**

- **Why it matters:** Only a valid AppSec attestation lets a repository outside a landing zone reach uat or prod.
- **Fix:** Ask AppSec to correct .kit/zone-readiness.json (the summary names the failed check) and approve it in a pull request.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/ZONE_READINESS_ATTESTATION.md](../adoption/ZONE_READINESS_ATTESTATION.md)

### READINESS_NOT_SET (readiness_source)

No readiness is set and there is no attestation file. **[READINESS_NOT_SET]**

- **Why it matters:** uat and prod releases are refused until readiness is established.
- **Fix:** Inside a landing zone, the platform team vends it; outside one, AppSec writes .kit/zone-readiness.json.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/ZONE_READINESS_ATTESTATION.md](../adoption/ZONE_READINESS_ATTESTATION.md)

### READINESS_SOURCE_SELF_SET_REFUSED (readiness_source)

KIT_ZONE_READINESS was set by the deploying team itself, with no landing-zone marker and no AppSec attestation. **[READINESS_SOURCE_SELF_SET_REFUSED]**

- **Why it matters:** A team cannot certify its own platform; refused at uat and prod.
- **Fix:** Delete the variable you set; ask AppSec for .kit/zone-readiness.json instead.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/ZONE_READINESS_ATTESTATION.md](../adoption/ZONE_READINESS_ATTESTATION.md)

### READINESS_SOURCE_TEST_FIXTURE (readiness_source)

The readiness value is a labelled test fixture, not a real readiness. **[READINESS_SOURCE_TEST_FIXTURE]**

- **Why it matters:** Allowed for testing, never an issued readiness.
- **Fix:** Nothing in a test repository; remove KIT_ZONE_READINESS_TEST_FIXTURE in a real one.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/ZONE_READINESS_ATTESTATION.md](../adoption/ZONE_READINESS_ATTESTATION.md)

## release_approval

Not failures (nothing to do): `RELEASE_APPROVAL_NOT_REQUIRED`, `RELEASE_APPROVAL_VERIFIED`.

### RELEASE_APPROVAL_ABSENT (release_approval)

Nobody approved this production deploy (an admin bypassed the review, or the environment has no reviewers). **[RELEASE_APPROVAL_ABSENT]**

- **Why it matters:** A uat or prod release needs a recorded approval by someone else; refused.
- **Fix:** Re-run the deploy and ask a reviewer from platform or security to approve it in the run page (Review deployments).
- **More:** [docs/adoption/SETUP.md](../adoption/SETUP.md)

### RELEASE_APPROVAL_NOT_BOUND_TO_DIGEST (release_approval)

The approval did not quote the image digest being released, so it is not shown to be for these exact bytes. **[RELEASE_APPROVAL_NOT_BOUND_TO_DIGEST]**

- **Why it matters:** Production approvals must name what they approve.
- **Fix:** Re-run and approve with a comment that contains the digest (or its first 12 hex characters); the summary shows it under "For the approver".
- **More:** [docs/adoption/SETUP.md](../adoption/SETUP.md)

### RELEASE_APPROVAL_NOT_ESTABLISHED (release_approval)

The deploy could not read who approved it, who requested it or who wrote the change. **[RELEASE_APPROVAL_NOT_ESTABLISHED]**

- **Why it matters:** An approval nobody can read is not an approval; refused.
- **Fix:** Check the deploy job has actions: read and that the commit author's email is linked to a GitHub account; re-run.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/SETUP.md](../adoption/SETUP.md)

### SELF_DEPLOYMENT_APPROVAL (release_approval)

The person who approved this release is the one who requested it, or the author of the change. **[SELF_DEPLOYMENT_APPROVAL]**

- **Why it matters:** Approving your own release is never accepted.
- **Fix:** Re-run and have a reviewer who is neither the requester nor the author approve it.
- **More:** [docs/ticketing/SEPARATION-OF-DUTIES.md](../ticketing/SEPARATION-OF-DUTIES.md)

## release_block

Not failures (nothing to do): `RELEASE_BLOCK_NOT_VENDED`, `RELEASE_NOT_BLOCKED`.

### RELEASE_BLOCKED_BY_PLATFORM (release_block)

The landing zone has paused releases to this workload (halted, expired, or over budget). **[RELEASE_BLOCKED_BY_PLATFORM]**

- **Why it matters:** Releases resume only when the platform lifts the stop; nothing was deployed.
- **Fix:** Ask the platform team why (the summary shows the value of KIT_RELEASE_BLOCK); do not change the variable yourself.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/LZ_KIT_HANDOFF_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/LZ_KIT_HANDOFF_CONTRACT.md)

## release_record

Not failures (nothing to do): `RELEASE_RECORD_KEPT`, `RELEASE_RECORD_KEPT_DEPLOYMENT`.

### RELEASE_RECORD_NOT_KEPT (release_record)

The deploy could not save its durable release record. **[RELEASE_RECORD_NOT_KEPT]**

- **Why it matters:** Without it, the release cannot be audited later; the step fails.
- **Fix:** Check the deploy job grants deployments: write (lease off) or that the lease store is reachable (lease on); re-run.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

## remediation_track_state

Not failures (nothing to do): `BREACHED_ACCEPTED`, `CLOSED_VERIFIED`, `ON_TRACK`.

### BREACHED_UNDECIDED (remediation_track_state)

A known finding is past its fix deadline and nobody has decided what to do. **[BREACHED_UNDECIDED]**

- **Why it matters:** Overdue findings owe a decision; after the grace period they block.
- **Fix:** Fix it, or ask its owner to record a dated decision.
- **More:** [docs/operations/FINDING_CLASSIFICATION.md](../operations/FINDING_CLASSIFICATION.md)

### TRACK_NOT_ADMITTED (remediation_track_state)

A known finding is not on a fix schedule (no fix status, severity or deadline recorded). **[TRACK_NOT_ADMITTED]**

- **Why it matters:** It cannot be tracked to closure.
- **Fix:** Ask the finding's owner to record its fix availability and deadline.
- **More:** [docs/operations/FINDING_CLASSIFICATION.md](../operations/FINDING_CLASSIFICATION.md)

### TRACK_STALLED (remediation_track_state)

No known finding in this repository has been fixed in the configured period. **[TRACK_STALLED]**

- **Why it matters:** A schedule nobody follows is not remediation.
- **Fix:** Fix at least the oldest findings; the promotion review asks for a decision.
- **More:** [docs/operations/FINDING_CLASSIFICATION.md](../operations/FINDING_CLASSIFICATION.md)

## reusable_workflow_resolution

Not failures (nothing to do): `CROSS_REPO`, `MATCHED`, `SAME_REPO`, `UNASSERTED`.

### MISMATCHED (reusable_workflow_resolution)

The workflow code that produced this evidence is not the code the caller said it expected. **[MISMATCHED]**

- **Why it matters:** A supply-chain mismatch: the kit pin or the caller is not what it claims.
- **Fix:** Check the uses: line pins the kit repository and SHA you intended.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/SETUP.md](../adoption/SETUP.md)

## review_finalize_state

Not failures (nothing to do): `REVIEW_FINALIZED`.

### REVIEW_NOT_FINALIZED (review_finalize_state)

The security review behind these tickets is not finalized with a recorded approval by a second person. **[REVIEW_NOT_FINALIZED]**

- **Why it matters:** Tickets are written only from a finalized, approved review; nothing was read or written.
- **Fix:** Have the concurring reviewer approve the review record's pull request and merge it; the summary lists each missing rule.
- **More:** [docs/ticketing/TICKET-TYPES.md](../ticketing/TICKET-TYPES.md)

## rollback_capability

Not failures (nothing to do): `AVAILABLE`, `NO_PRIOR_STATE`.

### UNAVAILABLE (rollback_capability)

If this deploy failed, it could not be undone (no usable previous version or no reversal mechanism). **[UNAVAILABLE]**

- **Why it matters:** At uat and prod a deploy that cannot be undone is refused.
- **Fix:** Enable multiple revisions (Container Apps) or a staging slot (App Service), or keep the previous artefact; then re-run.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md)

## rollback_dependency_check

Not failures (nothing to do): `DEPLOY_NO_ROLLBACK_DEPENDENCY`, `ROLLBACK_CHECK_NOT_REQUIRED`.

### DEPLOY_REFUSED_ROLLBACK_DEPENDENCY (rollback_dependency_check)

This deploy is built on something that was rolled back (a commit, an image or a dependency). **[DEPLOY_REFUSED_ROLLBACK_DEPENDENCY]**

- **Why it matters:** Deploying it would bring back what the rollback removed.
- **Fix:** Rebase onto the current main (after the rollback), rebuild and deploy; the report names each dependency.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md)

### ROLLBACK_DEPENDENCY_CHECK_INCOMPLETE (rollback_dependency_check)

The deploy could not check whether it depends on a recent rollback. **[ROLLBACK_DEPENDENCY_CHECK_INCOMPLETE]**

- **Why it matters:** Refused before changing anything.
- **Fix:** Re-run; if it persists, check the deploy job has actions: read.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md)

## rollback_dependency_outcome

Not failures (nothing to do): `ROLLBACK_DEPENDENCY_CLEAR`, `ROLLBACK_SCOPED_TO_PRODUCT_CONFIG`.

### ROLLBACK_PARTIAL_DEPENDENCY_CONFLICT (rollback_dependency_outcome)

Someone else changed part of what this release changed, so only the independent parts were rolled back. **[ROLLBACK_PARTIAL_DEPENDENCY_CONFLICT]**

- **Why it matters:** The rest is left as it is, each with its reason.
- **Fix:** Ask the platform team to review the remaining items.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md)

### ROLLBACK_REFUSED_DEPENDENCY_CONFLICT (rollback_dependency_outcome)

Everything this release changed was also changed by someone else, so nothing was rolled back. **[ROLLBACK_REFUSED_DEPENDENCY_CONFLICT]**

- **Why it matters:** Undoing it would overwrite another change.
- **Fix:** Ask the platform team to decide.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md)

### ROLLBACK_REFUSED_FOREIGN_EVIDENCE (rollback_dependency_outcome)

The evidence for a rollback step is not from a kit deploy of this target. **[ROLLBACK_REFUSED_FOREIGN_EVIDENCE]**

- **Why it matters:** The kit only rolls back its own releases.
- **Fix:** Check the run id in the sequence names a kit deploy of this target.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md)

### ROLLBACK_REFUSED_PLATFORM_OWNED (rollback_dependency_outcome)

The rollback would change a resource the landing zone owns (DNS, Front Door, network rules). **[ROLLBACK_REFUSED_PLATFORM_OWNED]**

- **Why it matters:** The kit never reverts platform resources.
- **Fix:** Ask the platform team; they own that change.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/LZ_KIT_SEAM_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/LZ_KIT_SEAM_CONTRACT.md)

## rollback_sequence

Not failures (nothing to do): `ROLLBACK_SEQUENCE_VERIFIED`.

### ROLLBACK_SEQUENCE_HALTED_E2E_FAILED (rollback_sequence)

After a step was rolled back, the end-to-end tests failed, so the sequence stopped. **[ROLLBACK_SEQUENCE_HALTED_E2E_FAILED]**

- **Why it matters:** A person decides the next step.
- **Fix:** Contact the platform team with the run link and the failing test.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md)

### ROLLBACK_SEQUENCE_HALTED_HEALTH_FAILED (rollback_sequence)

After a step was rolled back, the app's health check failed, so the sequence stopped. **[ROLLBACK_SEQUENCE_HALTED_HEALTH_FAILED]**

- **Why it matters:** Rolling back further could make it worse.
- **Fix:** Contact the platform team with the run link.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md)

### ROLLBACK_SEQUENCE_HALTED_ROLLBACK_UNVERIFIED (rollback_sequence)

A step's rollback did not complete cleanly, so the sequence stopped. **[ROLLBACK_SEQUENCE_HALTED_ROLLBACK_UNVERIFIED]**

- **Why it matters:** A partial rollback is never treated as done.
- **Fix:** Contact the platform team with the run link.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md)

### ROLLBACK_SEQUENCE_REFUSED_INPUT (rollback_sequence)

The rollback sequence or a step's deploy evidence could not be read, or did not fit together. **[ROLLBACK_SEQUENCE_REFUSED_INPUT]**

- **Why it matters:** Nothing was touched.
- **Fix:** Check the run ids in the sequence (the summary names the bad one) and re-run.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md)

### ROLLBACK_SEQUENCE_REFUSED_NO_E2E (rollback_sequence)

A rollback sequence was requested without an end-to-end test command. **[ROLLBACK_SEQUENCE_REFUSED_NO_E2E]**

- **Why it matters:** Untested reversals can break the user path; nothing was touched.
- **Fix:** Pass e2e_test_command (or set KIT_E2E_TEST_COMMAND) and re-run.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md)

### ROLLBACK_SEQUENCE_REFUSED_NO_TEST_PERIOD (rollback_sequence)

A rollback sequence was requested with an end-to-end test period of 0. **[ROLLBACK_SEQUENCE_REFUSED_NO_TEST_PERIOD]**

- **Why it matters:** Each step must be tested over a real period before the next; nothing was touched.
- **Fix:** Set the e2e test period (1-240 minutes) and re-run.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md)

### ROLLBACK_SEQUENCE_STOPPED_DEPENDENCY_CONFLICT (rollback_sequence)

A step's resources were changed by someone else since the release, so a full rollback was refused. **[ROLLBACK_SEQUENCE_STOPPED_DEPENDENCY_CONFLICT]**

- **Why it matters:** Undoing them would overwrite another team's change.
- **Fix:** Ask the platform team to resolve the conflict the summary names.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md)

### ROLLBACK_SEQUENCE_STOPPED_INELIGIBLE (rollback_sequence)

The sequence stopped before a step that is not safe to roll back. **[ROLLBACK_SEQUENCE_STOPPED_INELIGIBLE]**

- **Why it matters:** Earlier steps are rolled back and verified; that step and later ones are untouched.
- **Fix:** Ask the platform team to decide on the ineligible step (the summary names it).
- **More:** [docs/architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md)

## rollback_sequence_step

Not failures (nothing to do): `ROLLBACK_STEP_NOT_REACHED`, `ROLLBACK_STEP_VERIFIED`.

### ROLLBACK_STEP_HALTED (rollback_sequence_step)

This rollback step ran and did not hold (rollback, health or tests). **[ROLLBACK_STEP_HALTED]**

- **Why it matters:** The sequence stopped here.
- **Fix:** Contact the platform team with the run link.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md)

### ROLLBACK_STEP_INELIGIBLE (rollback_sequence_step)

This step was judged unsafe to roll back and was not touched. **[ROLLBACK_STEP_INELIGIBLE]**

- **Why it matters:** A person must decide.
- **Fix:** Contact the platform team with the run link.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md)

### ROLLBACK_STEP_PARTIAL (rollback_sequence_step)

Only the parts of this step that nobody else changed were rolled back. **[ROLLBACK_STEP_PARTIAL]**

- **Why it matters:** The rest is left for a person.
- **Fix:** Ask the platform team to review the remaining items.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md)

## rollback_state

Not failures (nothing to do): `AUTO_ROLLBACK_ALLOWED`, `ROLLBACK_VERIFIED`.

### ROLLBACK_PROHIBITED (rollback_state)

This change must not be undone; it can only be fixed forward. **[ROLLBACK_PROHIBITED]**

- **Why it matters:** Reversing it would be worse than the failure (for example a data migration).
- **Fix:** Fix forward: correct the code and deploy a new version.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md)

### ROLLBACK_REQUIRES_HUMAN_DECISION (rollback_state)

Undoing this change needs a person to decide: the previous state is unknown or reversal has consequences. **[ROLLBACK_REQUIRES_HUMAN_DECISION]**

- **Why it matters:** A machine should not weigh those consequences.
- **Fix:** Contact the platform team with the run link; do not re-run the deploy.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md)

### ROLLBACK_REQUIRES_VALIDATION (rollback_state)

The change can be undone, but the restored state must be proven correct before anyone calls it done. **[ROLLBACK_REQUIRES_VALIDATION]**

- **Why it matters:** A rollback that exits 0 is not a working service.
- **Fix:** Watch the verification in the summary; if it fails, escalate to the platform team.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.md)

## routing_result

Not failures (nothing to do): `PROCEED`.

### BLOCKED (routing_result)

The security scan stopped this change: a check found something that must be fixed first (for example a committed secret or a known-exploited vulnerability). **[BLOCKED]**

- **Why it matters:** Merging or deploying it would ship a problem the organisation has decided must never reach production.
- **Fix:** Open the run summary, find the blocking finding (file and line), fix it in your branch and push. A committed secret must also be revoked and rotated, not just deleted.
- **More:** [docs/security-review/READING-THE-RUN-SUMMARY.md](../security-review/READING-THE-RUN-SUMMARY.md)

### DECISION_REQUIRED (routing_result)

A person has to make a decision before this can deploy: a control was weakened without a recorded reason and owner, or an exception has expired. **[DECISION_REQUIRED]**

- **Why it matters:** The kit will not guess whether a weaker control is acceptable; an unexplained weakening is a decision nobody made.
- **Fix:** Either remove the weakening input from your workflow, or add all five fields (weakening_reason, weakening_authority, weakening_approver, weakening_exception_ref, weakening_expires) with a named approver who is not you.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### EVIDENCE_UNTRUSTED (routing_result)

The security scan could not finish properly, so its result cannot be trusted either way. **[EVIDENCE_UNTRUSTED]**

- **Why it matters:** A scanner that did not run is not a scanner that found nothing; treating it as clean would hide real problems.
- **Fix:** Re-run the workflow (Actions > the run > Re-run failed jobs). If it fails the same way, the summary names the scanner and the cause; send that to the platform team.
- **More:** [docs/operations/FAILURE_MODES.md](../operations/FAILURE_MODES.md)

### PROCEED_WITH_ADVISORY (routing_result)

The security scan passed with notes: it found things worth knowing that do not stop this change. **[PROCEED_WITH_ADVISORY]**

- **Why it matters:** Nothing is blocked, but each note is a real item someone should look at before it piles up; the run summary lists them.
- **Fix:** Open the run summary, read "Advisory causes", and fix or ticket each one. No action is needed to merge.
- **More:** [docs/security-review/READING-THE-RUN-SUMMARY.md](../security-review/READING-THE-RUN-SUMMARY.md)

## scan_examination

Not failures (nothing to do): `EXAMINED`.

### EXAMINED_NOTHING (scan_examination)

A scanner reported success but, by its own account, examined nothing. **[EXAMINED_NOTHING]**

- **Why it matters:** Zero findings from a scanner that read nothing is not a clean result.
- **Fix:** Open the scanner's summary: usually the files could not be parsed or no file matched; fix that and re-run.
- **More:** [docs/security-review/READING-THE-RUN-SUMMARY.md](../security-review/READING-THE-RUN-SUMMARY.md)

### NOT_DECLARED (scan_examination)

A scanner's report does not say what it examined. **[NOT_DECLARED]**

- **Why it matters:** The kit cannot count it as a clean scan.
- **Fix:** Re-run; if it repeats, report the scanner and its version to the platform team.
- **More:** [docs/operations/FAILURE_MODES.md](../operations/FAILURE_MODES.md)

## scan_partial_reason

### CODEQL_BUILD_PARTIAL (scan_partial_reason)

CodeQL's automatic build did not fully succeed, so part of the code may not have been analysed. **[CODEQL_BUILD_PARTIAL]**

- **Why it matters:** An unknown part of the code went unchecked.
- **Fix:** Make the project build with its standard command on ubuntu-latest (the CodeQL job log shows the build error).
- **More:** [docs/security-review/READING-THE-RUN-SUMMARY.md](../security-review/READING-THE-RUN-SUMMARY.md)

### CPP_ANALYSIS_PARTIAL (scan_partial_reason)

Some C/C++ files could not be analysed because the kit found no build information for them. **[CPP_ANALYSIS_PARTIAL]**

- **Why it matters:** The kit never invents a build system, so those files were not checked.
- **Fix:** Commit a compile_commands.json, or a top-level CMakeLists.txt or Makefile the kit can read.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### PARSE_PARTIAL_PHP_SYNTAX (scan_partial_reason)

Semgrep could not parse some PHP files, so those files were not checked; everything else was. **[PARSE_PARTIAL_PHP_SYNTAX]**

- **Why it matters:** Syntax it cannot read may hide a vulnerability.
- **Fix:** Open the sast-semgrep summary for the file list; fix the syntax or accept the gap (it does not block).
- **More:** [docs/security-review/READING-THE-RUN-SUMMARY.md](../security-review/READING-THE-RUN-SUMMARY.md)

## scanner_state

Not failures (nothing to do): `FINDINGS`, `NOT_APPLICABLE`, `PASS`.

### COLLECTION_FAILED (scanner_state)

A scanner ran, but its results could not be collected (the report was empty or unreadable). **[COLLECTION_FAILED]**

- **Why it matters:** An empty report looks exactly like a clean scan, so the kit refuses to treat it as one.
- **Fix:** Re-run the job; if it repeats, it is a pipeline defect: send the job log to the platform team.
- **More:** [docs/operations/FAILURE_MODES.md](../operations/FAILURE_MODES.md)

### FAILED (scanner_state)

A scanner crashed or exited with an error. **[FAILED]**

- **Why it matters:** Its findings were not established, so the run cannot be trusted as clean.
- **Fix:** Re-run the failed job; if it fails again, send the job log to the platform team.
- **More:** [docs/operations/FAILURE_MODES.md](../operations/FAILURE_MODES.md)

### PARTIAL (scanner_state)

A scanner ran but something it needed was missing, so it could not check everything. **[PARTIAL]**

- **Why it matters:** What it skipped is unchecked; the result is not a clean bill of health.
- **Fix:** Open the scanner's job summary for the missing prerequisite (a build file, a lockfile, a version) and add it.
- **More:** [docs/security-review/READING-THE-RUN-SUMMARY.md](../security-review/READING-THE-RUN-SUMMARY.md)

### UNAVAILABLE (scanner_state)

A scanner never ran on this run. **[UNAVAILABLE]**

- **Why it matters:** Nothing was checked by it, so the run cannot say the code is clean.
- **Fix:** The summary gives the reason (a download failure, a timeout, a licence); re-run, or pass the reason to the platform team.
- **More:** [docs/operations/FAILURE_MODES.md](../operations/FAILURE_MODES.md)

## seam_ownership_check

Not failures (nothing to do): `SEAM_OWNERSHIP_HELD`, `SEAM_OWNERSHIP_NOT_IN_FORCE`.

### SEAM_OWNERSHIP_NOT_ESTABLISHED (seam_ownership_check)

The deploy could not read the target's settings to check who owns them. **[SEAM_OWNERSHIP_NOT_ESTABLISHED]**

- **Why it matters:** Unknown ownership is not clear ownership; refused.
- **Fix:** Check the deploy identity can read app settings, and that KIT_SETTING_KEYS is a list of names; re-run.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/LZ_KIT_SEAM_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/LZ_KIT_SEAM_CONTRACT.md)

## seam_ownership_refusal

### SEAM_SETTING_OWNERSHIP_CONFLICT (seam_ownership_refusal)

The deploy would change an app setting the landing zone owns (or both sides claim it). **[SEAM_SETTING_OWNERSHIP_CONFLICT]**

- **Why it matters:** Each setting has one owner; nothing was written.
- **Fix:** Remove the key from KIT_SETTING_KEYS or ask the platform team to hand it over (the summary names the key).
- **More:** [docs/architecture/LZ_KIT_SEAM_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/LZ_KIT_SEAM_CONTRACT.md)

### SEAM_SWAP_MOVES_LZ_SETTING (seam_ownership_refusal)

An App Service slot swap would carry a landing-zone setting from one slot to the other. **[SEAM_SWAP_MOVES_LZ_SETTING]**

- **Why it matters:** That would change platform configuration; the swap is refused.
- **Fix:** Ask the platform team to make the setting sticky to its slot.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/LZ_KIT_SEAM_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/LZ_KIT_SEAM_CONTRACT.md)

## secret_exception_refusal

### EXCEPTION_HISTORY_TAMPERED (secret_exception_refusal)

Same meaning and fix as [`policy_resolution.EXCEPTION_HISTORY_TAMPERED`](#exception_history_tampered-policy_resolution).

### EXCEPTION_HISTORY_UNVERIFIED (secret_exception_refusal)

Same meaning and fix as [`policy_resolution.EXCEPTION_HISTORY_UNVERIFIED`](#exception_history_unverified-policy_resolution).

### EXCEPTION_RENEWAL_LIMIT (secret_exception_refusal)

Same meaning and fix as [`policy_resolution.EXCEPTION_RENEWAL_LIMIT`](#exception_renewal_limit-policy_resolution).

### SECRET_EXCEPTION_EXPIRED (secret_exception_refusal)

A secret exception has passed its expiry date. **[SECRET_EXCEPTION_EXPIRED]**

- **Why it matters:** Exceptions never renew by silence; the secret blocks again.
- **Fix:** Rotate and remove the secret, or ask the approver for a new expiry.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### SECRET_EXCEPTION_NOT_FINDING_SCOPED (secret_exception_refusal)

A secret exception does not name exactly one finding (its 12-character fingerprint). **[SECRET_EXCEPTION_NOT_FINDING_SCOPED]**

- **Why it matters:** An exception must cover one known secret, never a pattern; the secret still blocks.
- **Fix:** Put the finding's fingerprint (fp in the scan report) in the exception.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### SECRET_EXCEPTION_UNATTRIBUTED (secret_exception_refusal)

A secret exception is missing its explanation, approver or expiry (or, at uat/prod, the environment reviewers). **[SECRET_EXCEPTION_UNATTRIBUTED]**

- **Why it matters:** An exception nobody explained or approved is not an exception; the secret still blocks.
- **Fix:** Fill in explanation, approver, expires (and environment_reviewers for uat/prod).
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

### SECRET_EXCEPTION_UNTICKETED (secret_exception_refusal)

A secret exception has no valid work-item ticket (PROJECT-1234). **[SECRET_EXCEPTION_UNTICKETED]**

- **Why it matters:** Every exception must be traceable to a ticket; the secret still blocks.
- **Fix:** Add the ticket key to the exception's ticket field.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

## target_lease

Not failures (nothing to do): `LEASE_ACQUIRED`, `LEASE_BROKEN`, `LEASE_FENCE_PASSED`, `LEASE_MUTATION_MARKED`, `LEASE_NOT_IN_FORCE`, `LEASE_RELEASED`, `LEASE_STATUS`, `MUTATED_UNDER_LEASE`.

### BREAK_NOT_AUTHORISED (target_lease)

Someone outside the break authority tried to break the target's hold. **[BREAK_NOT_AUTHORISED]**

- **Why it matters:** Only the named break authority may do that, with a recorded reason.
- **Fix:** Ask the break authority (platform team) to do it.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/LZ_KIT_SEAM_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/LZ_KIT_SEAM_CONTRACT.md)

### LEASE_ABANDONED_MID_MUTATION (target_lease)

A previous run stopped in the middle of changing this target. **[LEASE_ABANDONED_MID_MUTATION]**

- **Why it matters:** The target's state is unknown; a person must decide before anyone deploys.
- **Fix:** Contact the platform team (the break authority) with the run link.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/LZ_KIT_SEAM_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/LZ_KIT_SEAM_CONTRACT.md)

### LEASE_EXPIRED_HOLDER (target_lease)

This run's hold on the target expired, so its change was not sent. **[LEASE_EXPIRED_HOLDER]**

- **Why it matters:** Another writer could take over at any moment.
- **Fix:** Re-run the deploy.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/LZ_KIT_SEAM_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/LZ_KIT_SEAM_CONTRACT.md)

### LEASE_HELD (target_lease)

Another pipeline (the landing zone or another run) is changing this target right now. **[LEASE_HELD]**

- **Why it matters:** Two writers at once could break it; this deploy stopped before changing anything.
- **Fix:** Wait for the other run to finish (the summary names it) and re-run.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/LZ_KIT_SEAM_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/LZ_KIT_SEAM_CONTRACT.md)

### LEASE_LOST (target_lease)

The deploy lost its hold on the target during a long step, so it stopped. **[LEASE_LOST]**

- **Why it matters:** Continuing without the hold could collide with another writer.
- **Fix:** Re-run; if it repeats, the platform team checks the lease store.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/LZ_KIT_SEAM_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/LZ_KIT_SEAM_CONTRACT.md)

### LEASE_NOT_HELD (target_lease)

The deploy tried to change the target without holding it; refused. **[LEASE_NOT_HELD]**

- **Why it matters:** Coordination is on for this environment and every change must hold the target.
- **Fix:** Re-run the whole deploy (it takes the hold first).
- **More:** [docs/architecture/LZ_KIT_SEAM_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/LZ_KIT_SEAM_CONTRACT.md)

### LEASE_STORE_UNREACHABLE (target_lease)

The deploy could not reach the store that coordinates deploys to this target. **[LEASE_STORE_UNREACHABLE]**

- **Why it matters:** It fails closed: nothing was changed.
- **Fix:** Run on a runner that reaches the lease storage account (runner_label), or ask the platform team; re-run.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/LZ_KIT_SEAM_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/LZ_KIT_SEAM_CONTRACT.md)

### LEASE_TARGET_NOT_VENDED (target_lease)

The coordination record for this target does not exist; the landing zone creates it with the target. **[LEASE_TARGET_NOT_VENDED]**

- **Why it matters:** Nothing was changed.
- **Fix:** Ask the platform team to vend the target's lease container.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/LZ_KIT_SEAM_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/LZ_KIT_SEAM_CONTRACT.md)

### MUTATED_WITHOUT_LEASE (target_lease)

The deploy lost its hold while a change was in flight; the change may have landed. **[MUTATED_WITHOUT_LEASE]**

- **Why it matters:** A person must decide whether to roll back.
- **Fix:** Contact the platform team with the run link.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/LZ_KIT_SEAM_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/LZ_KIT_SEAM_CONTRACT.md)

### MUTATION_FAILED (target_lease)

A change to the target failed while the deploy held it. **[MUTATION_FAILED]**

- **Why it matters:** The target is marked as mid-change so nobody takes it over automatically.
- **Fix:** Contact the platform team with the run link.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/LZ_KIT_SEAM_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/LZ_KIT_SEAM_CONTRACT.md)

### RELEASE_MID_MUTATION (target_lease)

A run tried to let go of the target while still changing it; refused. **[RELEASE_MID_MUTATION]**

- **Why it matters:** The hold never reads clean over a half-done change.
- **Fix:** Contact the platform team with the run link.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/LZ_KIT_SEAM_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/LZ_KIT_SEAM_CONTRACT.md)

### STALE_LEASE_HOLDER (target_lease)

This run's hold on the target was taken over or broken, so its change was not sent. **[STALE_LEASE_HOLDER]**

- **Why it matters:** Another writer owns the target now.
- **Fix:** Re-run the deploy once the target is free.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/LZ_KIT_SEAM_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/LZ_KIT_SEAM_CONTRACT.md)

## ticket_governance_state

Not failures (nothing to do): `AREA_RESOLVED`, `PROVENANCE_ESTABLISHED`, `TAG_PRESERVATION_ESTABLISHED`.

### AREA_UNRESOLVED (ticket_governance_state)

No routing rule gave this finding an owning area, so it waits in triage with an owner role and a deadline. **[AREA_UNRESOLVED]**

- **Why it matters:** A finding nobody owns is not worked; the triage owner must place it before the deadline.
- **Fix:** The owner role adds a ticket_routing rule that covers this kind of finding (or records why it has none).
- **More:** [docs/ticketing/TICKET-GOVERNANCE.md](../ticketing/TICKET-GOVERNANCE.md)

### AREA_UNRESOLVED_OVERDUE (ticket_governance_state)

A finding with no owning area is past its triage deadline. **[AREA_UNRESOLVED_OVERDUE]**

- **Why it matters:** It is still unowned; every run reports it until it is routed.
- **Fix:** Add a ticket_routing rule for it (the run names the owner role and the ticket).
- **More:** [docs/ticketing/TICKET-GOVERNANCE.md](../ticketing/TICKET-GOVERNANCE.md)

### CORRELATION_LABEL_COLLISION (ticket_governance_state)

A ticket carries this finding's label but its full key belongs to a different finding. **[CORRELATION_LABEL_COLLISION]**

- **Why it matters:** The full key is the only identity; a shared short label is a search ambiguity, not a match.
- **Fix:** A person checks both tickets; nothing is merged unless a reviewer links them.
- **More:** [docs/ticketing/TICKET-GOVERNANCE.md](../ticketing/TICKET-GOVERNANCE.md)

### CORRELATION_LABEL_UNVERIFIED (ticket_governance_state)

A ticket carries the finding's label but not its full key, so it was shown to a person instead of being linked. **[CORRELATION_LABEL_UNVERIFIED]**

- **Why it matters:** A label is only a search aid; linking on it alone could attach the finding to the wrong ticket.
- **Fix:** Confirm the link in a finalized review (link_decisions); the kit then writes the full key into the ticket.
- **More:** [docs/ticketing/TICKET-GOVERNANCE.md](../ticketing/TICKET-GOVERNANCE.md)

### PROVENANCE_MISMATCH (ticket_governance_state)

The integration named on the ticket (the via label) is not the identity that actually wrote it. **[PROVENANCE_MISMATCH]**

- **Why it matters:** A via label is a claim; a mismatch can mean a misconfigured integration or a ticket made to look automated.
- **Fix:** Check KIT_INTEGRATION_IDENTITIES and who created the ticket; correct the mapping or investigate the ticket.
- **More:** [docs/ticketing/TICKET-GOVERNANCE.md](../ticketing/TICKET-GOVERNANCE.md)

### PROVENANCE_NOT_ESTABLISHED (ticket_governance_state)

The kit could not confirm who wrote the ticket. **[PROVENANCE_NOT_ESTABLISHED]**

- **Why it matters:** Without the authenticated identity and the tracker's write record, the via claim is unproven.
- **Fix:** Give the tracker credential read access to the creator or activity history, and register the integration in KIT_INTEGRATION_IDENTITIES.
- **More:** [docs/ticketing/TICKET-GOVERNANCE.md](../ticketing/TICKET-GOVERNANCE.md)

### STAMP_FIELD_NOT_CONFIRMED (ticket_governance_state)

The new Freshservice ticket's key field did not save the full key. **[STAMP_FIELD_NOT_CONFIRMED]**

- **Why it matters:** The key field is how the kit finds the ticket again; the description still carries the key.
- **Fix:** Check FRESHSERVICE_STAMP_FIELD is a single-line text field on the ticket form.
- **More:** [docs/ticketing/TICKET-GOVERNANCE.md](../ticketing/TICKET-GOVERNANCE.md)

### TAG_PRESERVATION_NOT_ESTABLISHED (ticket_governance_state)

Freshservice replaced the ticket's whole tag list and the kit could not prove nobody else's tag change was lost. **[TAG_PRESERVATION_NOT_ESTABLISHED]**

- **Why it matters:** A person's tag may have been dropped by the kit's write.
- **Fix:** Check the ticket's tags against its activity history (the kit left a private note saying so).
- **More:** [docs/ticketing/TICKET-GOVERNANCE.md](../ticketing/TICKET-GOVERNANCE.md)

### TICKET_WRITE_LOCK_HELD (ticket_governance_state)

Another kit writer was updating the same ticket, so this write waited and then stopped. **[TICKET_WRITE_LOCK_HELD]**

- **Why it matters:** Two writers on one Freshservice ticket can overwrite each other's tags.
- **Fix:** Nothing to do; the next run makes the write. If it repeats, look for a stuck run.
- **More:** [docs/ticketing/TICKET-GOVERNANCE.md](../ticketing/TICKET-GOVERNANCE.md)

## ticket_intake_state

Not failures (nothing to do): `TRACKER_INTAKE_COMPLETE`.

### TRACKER_INTAKE_NOT_CONFIGURED (ticket_intake_state)

The kit cannot search this tracker for existing tickets. **[TRACKER_INTAKE_NOT_CONFIGURED]**

- **Why it matters:** Duplicates cannot be found before creating.
- **Fix:** Use Jira for work tickets (the kit's supported tracker).
- **More:** [docs/architecture/TICKETING_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/TICKETING_CONTRACT.md)

### TRACKER_INTAKE_PARTIAL (ticket_intake_state)

The search of existing tickets did not finish. **[TRACKER_INTAKE_PARTIAL]**

- **Why it matters:** Tickets not read are not absent; new tickets are created in triage to be checked again.
- **Fix:** Re-run later; check the tracker credential if it repeats.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/TICKETING_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/TICKETING_CONTRACT.md)

### TRACKER_QUERY_REFUSED (ticket_intake_state)

A ticket search named a project outside this repository's projects, or used a forbidden query clause. **[TRACKER_QUERY_REFUSED]**

- **Why it matters:** Searches are limited to this repository's projects.
- **Fix:** Search only this repository's ticket projects, without ORDER BY.
- **More:** [docs/api/README.md](../api/README.md)

## ticket_lookup_outcome

Not failures (nothing to do): `BACKEND_BOUND`, `BINDING_ABSENT`, `LEDGER_BOUND`.

### BINDING_AMBIGUOUS (ticket_lookup_outcome)

More than one ticket claims the same finding, so the kit updated none of them. **[BINDING_AMBIGUOUS]**

- **Why it matters:** Picking one would be a guess.
- **Fix:** Close the duplicate tickets (each is named in the summary) so one remains.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/TICKETING_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/TICKETING_CONTRACT.md)

### BINDING_DANGLING (ticket_lookup_outcome)

A ticket the kit recorded for a finding could not be found (deleted, moved or no access). **[BINDING_DANGLING]**

- **Why it matters:** A missing ticket is not proof the work is done; nothing new was created.
- **Fix:** Restore or re-link the ticket, or check the credential can see that project.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/TICKETING_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/TICKETING_CONTRACT.md)

### BINDING_UNESTABLISHED (ticket_lookup_outcome)

The ticket search did not finish (rate limit, outage or expired credential). **[BINDING_UNESTABLISHED]**

- **Why it matters:** Without a complete search the kit cannot tell whether a ticket exists, so it creates none.
- **Fix:** Re-run later; check the tracker credential if it repeats.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/TICKETING_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/TICKETING_CONTRACT.md)

### IDENTITY_NOT_ESTABLISHED (ticket_lookup_outcome)

A finding has no stable identity, so no ticket can be looked up or created for it. **[IDENTITY_NOT_ESTABLISHED]**

- **Why it matters:** A ticket on an unstable identity would be duplicated every run.
- **Fix:** Nothing for you; the summary lists the finding for a person to triage.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/TICKETING_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/TICKETING_CONTRACT.md)

## ticket_reference_outcome

Not failures (nothing to do): `REFERENCE_FOUND`.

### NOT_A_PULL_REQUEST (ticket_reference_outcome)

The ticket-reference check ran on something that is not a pull request, so it checked nothing. **[NOT_A_PULL_REQUEST]**

- **Why it matters:** Not assessed is not passed.
- **Fix:** Nothing; it only applies to pull requests.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/JIRA_AUTH_AND_ROUTING.md](../architecture/JIRA_AUTH_AND_ROUTING.md)

### NO_CANDIDATE (ticket_reference_outcome)

The pull request description does not mention a ticket. **[NO_CANDIDATE]**

- **Why it matters:** Every change must link to its work item.
- **Fix:** Add the ticket key (for example PROJ-1234) to the pull request description.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/JIRA_AUTH_AND_ROUTING.md](../architecture/JIRA_AUTH_AND_ROUTING.md)

### NO_CANDIDATE_PASSED (ticket_reference_outcome)

The pull request mentions a ticket, but its number is outside the allowed range. **[NO_CANDIDATE_PASSED]**

- **Why it matters:** The check accepts only references that look like your tracker's real keys.
- **Fix:** Edit the pull request description to use the full ticket key (for example PROJ-1234).
- **More:** [docs/architecture/JIRA_AUTH_AND_ROUTING.md](../architecture/JIRA_AUTH_AND_ROUTING.md)

### NO_TEXT (ticket_reference_outcome)

The pull request description is empty. **[NO_TEXT]**

- **Why it matters:** There was nothing to search for a ticket key.
- **Fix:** Write a description that includes the ticket key.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/JIRA_AUTH_AND_ROUTING.md](../architecture/JIRA_AUTH_AND_ROUTING.md)

### POLICY_MISCONFIGURED (ticket_reference_outcome)

The ticket-number range in the workflow is set up wrongly (one bound missing, not a number, or reversed). **[POLICY_MISCONFIGURED]**

- **Why it matters:** The check could not run; this is a platform setting, not your pull request.
- **Fix:** Ask the workflow owner to fix the min/max digit inputs of the ticket-reference job.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/JIRA_AUTH_AND_ROUTING.md](../architecture/JIRA_AUTH_AND_ROUTING.md)

## ticket_template_outcome

Not failures (nothing to do): `TEMPLATE_CLOSED_DUPLICATE`, `TEMPLATE_FIX_OBSERVED`, `TEMPLATE_LINKED_EXACT`, `TEMPLATE_PENDING_VERIFICATION`, `TEMPLATE_POSSIBLE_DUPLICATE`, `TEMPLATE_REGRESSION`, `TEMPLATE_REOPENED_AS_REMEDIATION`, `TEMPLATE_TICKET_BOUND`, `TEMPLATE_TICKET_CLOSED`, `TEMPLATE_TICKET_CREATED`, `TEMPLATE_TICKET_PLANNED`, `TEMPLATE_TICKET_UPDATED`, `TEMPLATE_TRIAGED_SEPARATE`.

### TEMPLATE_DEDUPE_PENDING (ticket_template_outcome)

The duplicate search did not finish, so the ticket was created in triage marked dedupe-pending. **[TEMPLATE_DEDUPE_PENDING]**

- **Why it matters:** It is never lost; the next run checks it again.
- **Fix:** Nothing; a person triages it if the next run still cannot.
- **More:** [docs/ticketing/TICKET-TYPES.md](../ticketing/TICKET-TYPES.md)

### TEMPLATE_OUTBOX (ticket_template_outcome)

The tracker could not be written, so the item was kept in the outbox for the next run. **[TEMPLATE_OUTBOX]**

- **Why it matters:** Nothing is lost; a person was alerted.
- **Fix:** Check the tracker credential; the next run retries first.
- **More:** [docs/ticketing/TICKET-TYPES.md](../ticketing/TICKET-TYPES.md)

### TEMPLATE_SENT_BACK (ticket_template_outcome)

The concurring reviewer disagreed with this item, so nothing was written for it. **[TEMPLATE_SENT_BACK]**

- **Why it matters:** Their dissent is recorded.
- **Fix:** Discuss with the reviewer and resubmit if agreed.
- **More:** [docs/ticketing/TICKET-TYPES.md](../ticketing/TICKET-TYPES.md)

### TEMPLATE_VERIFICATION_REJECTED (ticket_template_outcome)

A verifier rejected the fix, so the ticket was reopened. **[TEMPLATE_VERIFICATION_REJECTED]**

- **Why it matters:** The fix did not hold.
- **Fix:** Read the verifier's reason on the ticket and fix again.
- **More:** [docs/ticketing/TICKET-TYPES.md](../ticketing/TICKET-TYPES.md)

## ticket_template_refusal

### CHILD_OBLIGATION_OPEN (ticket_template_refusal)

The multicloud ticket cannot close yet: a child obligation (Azure or AWS) is still open. **[CHILD_OBLIGATION_OPEN]**

- **Why it matters:** Each cloud has its own owner and its own fix; the parent closes only when every child is verified.
- **Fix:** Close each child ticket first (its owner resolves it; a rescan or another person verifies it); the parent then closes itself.
- **More:** [docs/ticketing/TICKET-GOVERNANCE.md](../ticketing/TICKET-GOVERNANCE.md)

### CLOSURE_NOT_VERIFIED (ticket_template_refusal)

A closure was requested but the kit's scan does not show the finding fixed. **[CLOSURE_NOT_VERIFIED]**

- **Why it matters:** Tickets close only on verified fixes.
- **Fix:** Merge the fix to the mapped branch and let the scan run, then close.
- **More:** [docs/ticketing/TICKET-TYPES.md](../ticketing/TICKET-TYPES.md)

### EXCEPTION_TOO_LONG (ticket_template_refusal)

An exception asked for longer than the maximum (90 days). **[EXCEPTION_TOO_LONG]**

- **Why it matters:** Exceptions are always time-limited.
- **Fix:** Request 90 days or less.
- **More:** [docs/ticketing/TICKET-TYPES.md](../ticketing/TICKET-TYPES.md)

### EXTENSION_CEILING_EXCEEDED (ticket_template_refusal)

The requested new expiry is further out than one extension allows. **[EXTENSION_CEILING_EXCEEDED]**

- **Why it matters:** Each extension is limited.
- **Fix:** Request an expiry within the ceiling.
- **More:** [docs/ticketing/TICKET-TYPES.md](../ticketing/TICKET-TYPES.md)

### EXTENSION_COUNT_MISMATCH (ticket_template_refusal)

The number of extensions claimed differs from what the ticket's labels show. **[EXTENSION_COUNT_MISMATCH]**

- **Why it matters:** History is never shortened.
- **Fix:** Use the count the ticket shows.
- **More:** [docs/ticketing/TICKET-TYPES.md](../ticketing/TICKET-TYPES.md)

### EXTENSION_LIMIT_REACHED (ticket_template_refusal)

The ticket has had the maximum number of extensions. **[EXTENSION_LIMIT_REACHED]**

- **Why it matters:** It cannot be extended again.
- **Fix:** Fix the finding, or ask the owner for an accepted-risk decision.
- **More:** [docs/ticketing/TICKET-TYPES.md](../ticketing/TICKET-TYPES.md)

### LINK_DECISION_INVALID (ticket_template_refusal)

A link decision names a finding, ticket or candidate that does not exist in the request. **[LINK_DECISION_INVALID]**

- **Why it matters:** Links must point at real candidates.
- **Fix:** Link only tickets the search returned.
- **More:** [docs/ticketing/TICKET-TYPES.md](../ticketing/TICKET-TYPES.md)

### NOFIX_EXEMPTION_TOO_LONG (ticket_template_refusal)

A no-fix re-check asked for an automatic exemption longer than allowed. **[NOFIX_EXEMPTION_TOO_LONG]**

- **Why it matters:** Longer exemptions need a person to accept the risk.
- **Fix:** Shorten the exemption, or request an accepted risk.
- **More:** [docs/ticketing/TICKET-TYPES.md](../ticketing/TICKET-TYPES.md)

### SOD_SELF_APPROVAL (ticket_template_refusal)

The person approving is the author of what is being approved. **[SOD_SELF_APPROVAL]**

- **Why it matters:** Nobody approves their own exception, triage or fix.
- **Fix:** Have another approver from the list approve it.
- **More:** [docs/ticketing/SEPARATION-OF-DUTIES.md](../ticketing/SEPARATION-OF-DUTIES.md)

### TEMPLATE_ASSET_IDENTITY_INVALID (ticket_template_refusal)

The asset named in a ticket item is not a valid identity (wrong subscription, account or a missing field). **[TEMPLATE_ASSET_IDENTITY_INVALID]**

- **Why it matters:** Tickets must point at a real, owned asset.
- **Fix:** Correct the asset id the refusal names.
- **More:** [docs/ticketing/TICKET-TYPES.md](../ticketing/TICKET-TYPES.md)

### TEMPLATE_FIELD_INVALID (ticket_template_refusal)

A ticket item breaks its template (a missing field, a bad value, or an expiry in the past). **[TEMPLATE_FIELD_INVALID]**

- **Why it matters:** Only complete, valid items are written.
- **Fix:** Correct the field the refusal names.
- **More:** [docs/ticketing/TICKET-TYPES.md](../ticketing/TICKET-TYPES.md)

### TEMPLATE_NOT_ENABLED (ticket_template_refusal)

The template is proposed and not enabled yet. **[TEMPLATE_NOT_ENABLED]**

- **Why it matters:** Disabled templates are refused.
- **Fix:** Use an enabled template, or ask the owner to enable it.
- **More:** [docs/ticketing/TICKET-TYPES.md](../ticketing/TICKET-TYPES.md)

### TEMPLATE_UNKNOWN (ticket_template_refusal)

The ticket template named is not one the kit serves. **[TEMPLATE_UNKNOWN]**

- **Why it matters:** Unknown templates are refused.
- **Fix:** Use a template listed in docs/ticketing/TICKET-TYPES.md.
- **More:** [docs/ticketing/TICKET-TYPES.md](../ticketing/TICKET-TYPES.md)
