### TEMPLATE_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED (ticket_template_refusal)

The ticket template version is not supported (version 2 is current). **[TEMPLATE_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED]**

- **Why it matters:** Old versions are superseded.
- **Fix:** Set template_version to 2.
- **More:** [docs/ticketing/TICKET-TYPES.md](../ticketing/TICKET-TYPES.md)

### TICKET_NOT_KIT_LINKED (ticket_template_refusal)

An extension or closure names a ticket the kit does not own or link. **[TICKET_NOT_KIT_LINKED]**

- **Why it matters:** The kit changes only its own tickets.
- **Fix:** Update that ticket in the tracker directly.
- **More:** [docs/ticketing/TICKET-TYPES.md](../ticketing/TICKET-TYPES.md)

## ticketing_availability

Not failures (nothing to do): `TICKETING_AVAILABLE`.

### TICKETING_NOT_CONFIGURED (ticketing_availability)

No ticket tracker is configured (or two are), so no tickets were created or checked. **[TICKETING_NOT_CONFIGURED]**

- **Why it matters:** Findings that need tickets did not get them.
- **Fix:** Set the tracker secrets in the ticketing environment (docs/adoption/SETUP.md, ticketing) and the backend input to jira.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/SETUP.md](../adoption/SETUP.md)

### TICKETING_TEST_TARGETS_REAL_PROJECT (ticketing_availability)

A test ticketing run (from a branch other than main) was pointed at a real Jira project, so nothing was sent. **[TICKETING_TEST_TARGETS_REAL_PROJECT]**

- **Why it matters:** Test runs must never create tickets in real projects.
- **Fix:** Point the sandbox environment's JIRA_PROJECT at a test project, or run from main.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/JIRA_AUTH_AND_ROUTING.md](../architecture/JIRA_AUTH_AND_ROUTING.md)

### TICKETING_UNAVAILABLE (ticketing_availability)

The ticket tracker could not be reached, refused the credentials, or a write failed. **[TICKETING_UNAVAILABLE]**

- **Why it matters:** Tickets owed this run are carried forward; nothing is concluded from what was not read.
- **Fix:** Check JIRA_EMAIL, JIRA_TOKEN and JIRA_HOST in the ticketing environment (a token may have expired), then re-run.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/JIRA_AUTH_AND_ROUTING.md](../architecture/JIRA_AUTH_AND_ROUTING.md)

## tier_reality

Not failures (nothing to do): `TIER_CONSISTENT`.

### TIER_MISMATCH_SUSPECTED (tier_reality)

An environment marked dev or test looks like production (a custom domain, or production-like scale). **[TIER_MISMATCH_SUSPECTED]**

- **Why it matters:** Production traffic may be getting dev-level checks.
- **Fix:** Check KIT_ENVIRONMENT_TIER for this environment; if it serves real users, mark it uat or prod.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/LZ_KIT_HANDOFF_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/LZ_KIT_HANDOFF_CONTRACT.md)

### TIER_REALITY_UNREAD (tier_reality)

The deploy could not read whether the target looks like production. **[TIER_REALITY_UNREAD]**

- **Why it matters:** A missing signal, recorded so a reviewer knows.
- **Fix:** Nothing usually; it follows an earlier refusal in the same run.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/LZ_KIT_HANDOFF_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/LZ_KIT_HANDOFF_CONTRACT.md)

## tier_source

Not failures (nothing to do): `TIER_VENDED`.

### TIER_SELF_DECLARED (tier_source)

The environment's tier (dev, test, uat, prod) was set by the team, not by the landing zone. **[TIER_SELF_DECLARED]**

- **Why it matters:** The tier decides how strict the deploy is; a self-declared tier is recorded so reviewers can see it.
- **Fix:** Inside a landing zone, ask the platform team to vend KIT_ENVIRONMENT_TIER.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/LZ_KIT_HANDOFF_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/LZ_KIT_HANDOFF_CONTRACT.md)

## unknown_id_review

### MAPPING_NOT_REVIEWED (unknown_id_review)

An id mapping has no author, date or review reference, so it was refused. **[MAPPING_NOT_REVIEWED]**

- **Why it matters:** Mappings change how findings are grouped; each must be reviewed.
- **Fix:** Add author, date and review_ref to the mapping in id-mappings.json.
- **More:** [docs/operations/FINDING_CLASSIFICATION.md](../operations/FINDING_CLASSIFICATION.md)

### NEEDS_MAPPING (unknown_id_review)

An id the kit could not read is waiting for a person to map it. **[NEEDS_MAPPING]**

- **Why it matters:** The finding is still a finding; only its id is unmapped.
- **Fix:** The platform team maps it in id-mappings.json with a review reference.
- **More:** [docs/operations/FINDING_CLASSIFICATION.md](../operations/FINDING_CLASSIFICATION.md)

## verdict_provenance

Not failures (nothing to do): `MANUAL_REVIEW_VERDICT`, `VERDICT_FROM_GATE`.

### TYPED_VERDICT (verdict_provenance)

The deploy was handed a verdict that no security scan produced (it was typed in). **[TYPED_VERDICT]**

- **Why it matters:** A typed verdict is refused at uat and prod unless AppSec recorded a manual review.
- **Fix:** Deploy from a run that ran the security scan, or have AppSec fill manual_review_by, manual_review_ref and manual_review_date.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### VERDICT_CONTRADICTED (verdict_provenance)

The verdict handed to the deploy is more permissive than what the security scan actually decided. **[VERDICT_CONTRADICTED]**

- **Why it matters:** A deploy cannot be told "pass" when the scan said otherwise; refused at every tier.
- **Fix:** Pass the security job's own routing_result and advisory_causes to the deploy, unchanged.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### VERDICT_RECORD_UNREADABLE (verdict_provenance)

The deploy could not read the security scan's record for the run its verdict came from. **[VERDICT_RECORD_UNREADABLE]**

- **Why it matters:** An unreadable record is not "no record"; refused at uat and prod.
- **Fix:** Check the security run still has its kit-security-record artifact (retention) and the deploy job has actions: read.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

## version_applicability

Not failures (nothing to do): `NOT_SELECTED`, `SCANNER_SUPPORTS`, `VERSION_DISCOVERED`.

### PLATFORM_UNAVAILABLE (version_applicability)

A scanner that could read this code was withdrawn by the platform on this repository (for example code scanning unavailable). **[PLATFORM_UNAVAILABLE]**

- **Why it matters:** That check did not run; it is a platform decision.
- **Fix:** Nothing for you; the platform team decides.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### VERSION_GAP (version_applicability)

Same meaning and fix as [`advisory_cause.VERSION_GAP`](#version_gap-advisory_cause).

### VERSION_SUPPORT_UNDETERMINED (version_applicability)

The kit could not tell whether a scanner can read the language version this code targets. **[VERSION_SUPPORT_UNDETERMINED]**

- **Why it matters:** The result for that part is uncertain.
- **Fix:** Pin the version explicitly (for example .python-version, global.json, go.mod's go line) so the kit can read it.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### VERSION_UNSUPPORTED (version_applicability)

A scanner cannot read the language version this code targets. **[VERSION_UNSUPPORTED]**

- **Why it matters:** That scanner's part was not checked; another may substitute.
- **Fix:** Move to a supported version (docs/adoption/USAGE.md lists them) or accept the advisory.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

## version_gap_ruling

Not failures (nothing to do): `VERSION_GAP_EXCEPTION_ACCEPTED`, `VERSION_GAP_NOT_ENGAGED`, `VERSION_GAP_RECORDED`, `VERSION_GAP_UNVERIFIED_RECORDED`.

### ADVISORY_CAUSE_UNKNOWN (version_gap_ruling)

A uat or prod deploy was given an advisory verdict without the reason for it. **[ADVISORY_CAUSE_UNKNOWN]**

- **Why it matters:** The deploy cannot judge an advisory it cannot read.
- **Fix:** Pass advisory_causes from the security job to the deploy job (the template passes needs.security.outputs.advisory_causes).
- **More:** [docs/adoption/USAGE.md](../adoption/USAGE.md)

### VERSION_GAP_REFUSED (version_gap_ruling)

A uat or prod deploy was refused because part of the code could not be scanned at its version, and nobody accepted that gap. **[VERSION_GAP_REFUSED]**

- **Why it matters:** Production gets only code the scanners could read, or a named person's accepted exception.
- **Fix:** Upgrade to a supported version, or deploy with all five weakening fields filled in by an approver who is not you.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md](../adoption/POLICY_REGISTER.md)

## zone_readiness

Not failures (nothing to do): `READY`.

### NOT_READY (zone_readiness)

The landing zone for this environment failed a readiness check. **[NOT_READY]**

- **Why it matters:** The zone may take nothing beyond dev until it is fixed.
- **Fix:** Ask the platform team which readiness gate failed.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/LZ_KIT_HANDOFF_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/LZ_KIT_HANDOFF_CONTRACT.md)

### READY_WITH_EXCEPTIONS (zone_readiness)

The landing zone is ready with recorded exceptions; uat and prod releases proceed with a warning. **[READY_WITH_EXCEPTIONS]**

- **Why it matters:** Some readiness checks have approved exceptions.
- **Fix:** Nothing for you; the platform team owns the exceptions.
- **More:** [docs/architecture/LZ_KIT_HANDOFF_CONTRACT.md](../architecture/LZ_KIT_HANDOFF_CONTRACT.md)

### UNKNOWN (zone_readiness)

Nobody has established whether the landing zone is ready (the value is unset or unrecognised). **[UNKNOWN]**

- **Why it matters:** uat and prod releases are refused until it is known.
- **Fix:** Inside a landing zone, ask the platform team to vend KIT_ZONE_READINESS; outside one, AppSec writes .kit/zone-readiness.json.
- **More:** [docs/adoption/ZONE_READINESS_ATTESTATION.md](../adoption/ZONE_READINESS_ATTESTATION.md)

## zone_readiness_gate

Not failures (nothing to do): `ZONE_READINESS_NOT_REQUIRED`, `ZONE_READINESS_PERMITTED`.

### RELEASE_REFUSED_ZONE_NOT_READY (zone_readiness_gate)

A uat or prod release was refused because the target zone is not ready, or its readiness is unknown. **[RELEASE_REFUSED_ZONE_NOT_READY]**

- **Why it matters:** Production releases need a zone that passed its readiness checks.
- **Fix:** Inside a landing zone, ask the platform team; outside one, AppSec adds .kit/zone-readiness.json (docs/adoption/ZONE_READINESS_ATTESTATION.md).
- **More:** [docs/adoption/ZONE_READINESS_ATTESTATION.md](../adoption/ZONE_READINESS_ATTESTATION.md)

## Namespaces with no developer-facing failures

These taxonomy namespaces hold vocabulary a developer never sees as a run outcome. Each says why.

| namespace | why it is not here |
|---|---|
| `app_team_check` | a recorded note beside environment_protection; only its refusal, ENVIRONMENT_APPROVERS_ALL_APP_TEAM, is shown to developers |
| `capability_maturity` | how far a kit capability is proven, read by kit maintainers and reviewers |
| `capability_metadata` | capability-specific facts carried beside the shared vocabulary, not outcomes |
| `capability_origin` | where a kit capability came from, read by kit maintainers |
| `change_artefact` | the records a deploy keeps about a change, a field of the rollback model |
| `compliance_review_type` | the compliance review a finding class implies, a field of the ticket model |
| `content_normalisation_policy` | how a matched construct is normalised before hashing, internal to identity |
| `corpus_family_outcome` | the outcome of a kit scanner-corpus probe, run by kit maintainers only |
| `cost_measurement_state` | what the kit's cost measurement can say, read by kit maintainers |
| `credential_redaction` | a rule about redaction with no values of its own |
| `deferral_obligation` | whether a recorded deferral is in force, reported inside ticket records |
| `disposition_carry` | how an approved exception reached a finding, internal to the register reader |
| `disposition_type` | the four kinds of approved decision about a finding, a field of the register |
| `enforcement_rung` | the rung names (crawl, walk, run), configuration rather than an outcome |
| `environment_tier` | the tier names themselves (sandbox to prod), configuration rather than an outcome |
| `epistemic_property` | words for dashboards and reports about coverage, never a run outcome |
| `evidence_confidence` | how strongly a capability claim is supported, read by kit maintainers |
| `finding_classification` | how a maintainer classifies a red kit result before changing anything |
| `finding_confidence` | how strongly evidence supports a ticket cluster, a field of the ticket model |
| `finding_identity_match` | matching a finding against the baseline ledger, internal to the gate |
| `finding_subject` | what a finding is about, a field of the evidence model, not an outcome |
| `fix_availability` | whether a finding can be fixed, a field of the remediation record |
| `handoff_write_refusal` | the landing zone's own refusal, which the kit cites and never emits |
| `human_approval` | whether a person permitted one ticket mutation, internal to the reconciler |
| `iac_mode` | an input value (auto, disabled, required); a disabled one is reported as discovery_state.DISABLED |
| `identity_proof_failure` | the failure words of one kit proof, seen only by kit maintainers |
| `identity_refusal` | why a durable finding identity was not computed, read by the ledger and its proofs |
| `identity_scope` | how far a finding identity may be trusted, a field of the evidence model |
| `kit_api_data` | words the API writes inside result data, not refusals |
| `lineage_attribution` | who asserted a lineage link, recorded on ledger events for maintainers |
| `lineage_cause` | why an identity moved, recorded on ledger events for maintainers |
| `lineage_ledger_integrity` | whether the lineage ledger chain verifies, checked by kit maintainers |
| `lineage_proof_failure` | the failure words of one kit proof, seen only by kit maintainers |
| `lineage_relation` | how finding identities relate across an identity change, internal to the ledger |
| `lineage_resolution` | what an identity resolves to now, internal to the ledger |
| `lz_drift_class` | the landing zone's drift severity, emitted by the deployed scan for the platform team |
| `lz_drift_dimension` | the landing zone's drift vocabulary, emitted by the deployed scan for the platform team |
| `mutation_class` | which ticket mutations need a person, internal to the reconciler |
| `observation_quality` | what a kit control knows about its own channel, read by the kit and its proofs |
| `policy_mode` | derived from the rung, never set or seen as a refusal (lowercase mode names) |
| `projection` | a rule about how consumers reduce evidence, with no values of its own |
| `promotion_approval` | a field inside the promotion record, explained by release_approval refusals |
| `promotion_record_state` | a field inside the promotion record, explained by promotion_gate refusals |
| `provenance_identity` | a rule about binding identity at capture, with no values of its own |
| `release_ownership` | per-object attribution read during a reversal, internal to the rollback contract |
| `reversal_conflict` | why one reversal entry could not be actioned, internal to the rollback contract |
| `reversal_disposition` | what recovery may do to one object, internal to the rollback contract |
| `rollback_resource_class` | how a rollback treats one Azure resource type, a registry field |
| `rollback_step_eligibility` | why a rollback step was eligible, an explanation not a refusal |
| `scan_depth` | how hard a scan looks by trigger (pr, merge, nightly ...), configuration rather than an outcome |
| `seam_field_drift` | a CANDIDATE vocabulary of the landing zone's seam detector, not emitted by the kit |
| `selftest_reach` | how the kit's own CI exercises a workflow, read by kit maintainers |
| `suppression_reason` | recorded per error-suppressing line of kit code, read by kit maintainers |
| `task_state` | the lifecycle of a child task inside the tracker, not a run outcome |
| `team_pattern` | team-size names, configuration rather than an outcome |
| `ticket_class` | what a ticket asks for, a field of the ticket model |
| `ticket_closure_rule` | how ticket closure is evaluated, a field of the ticket model |
| `ticket_state` | the lifecycle of a parent ticket inside the tracker, not a run outcome |
| `ticket_trigger` | why a ticket was raised, a field of the ticket model |
| `toolchain_currency` | declared but not implemented; no run emits it |
| `transition_reason` | why a release moved, recorded on the transition for audit |
| `untrusted_input_transport` | how a value reaches a script body, checked by the kit's own lint |
| `validation_debt_state` | how an unproven kit capability is held, read by kit maintainers |
